=== STEP 3 — Data migration (no schema.prisma change)
- Create apps/backend/prisma/migrations/20260930190000_budget_range_from_estimate/migration.sql. If E-client-3 already added a later timestamp, pick a timestamp after the newest folder.
- SQL (the Postgres enum types are "budget_range" and "project_size"):
```
WITH d AS (
  SELECT r.id,
    (CASE WHEN r.budget_estimate_ron < 5000 THEN 'UNDER_5K'
          WHEN r.budget_estimate_ron <= 15000 THEN 'FROM_5K_TO_15K'
          ELSE 'OVER_15K' END)::"budget_range" AS new_range,
    (r.status IN ('IN_MARKETPLACE','CLAIMED_PARTIAL','EXPIRED') AND r.size_score IS NOT NULL) AS rescore,
    r.size_score - COALESCE((SELECT c.weight FROM project_sizing_config c WHERE c.key='BUDGET' AND c.option=r.budget_range::text),0) AS base_plus
  FROM requests r
  WHERE r.deleted_at IS NULL AND r.budget_estimate_ron IS NOT NULL
    AND r.budget_range IS NOT NULL AND r.budget_range <> 'UNDISCLOSED'
), d2 AS (
  SELECT d.*, d.base_plus + COALESCE((SELECT c.weight FROM project_sizing_config c WHERE c.key='BUDGET' AND c.option=d.new_range::text),0) AS new_score
  FROM d
)
UPDATE requests r SET
  budget_range = d2.new_range,
  size_score = CASE WHEN d2.rescore THEN d2.new_score ELSE r.size_score END,
  project_size = CASE WHEN d2.rescore THEN COALESCE(
      (SELECT t.size FROM project_size_thresholds t WHERE d2.new_score >= t.min_score AND (t.max_score IS NULL OR d2.new_score <= t.max_score) ORDER BY t.min_score LIMIT 1),
      (SELECT t.size FROM project_size_thresholds t ORDER BY t.min_score DESC LIMIT 1))
    ELSE r.project_size END
FROM d2 WHERE r.id = d2.id AND r.budget_range <> d2.new_range;
```

plan.summary: Plan for E-client-3 (Sprint 7, P1, 2 days). (1) Add an authenticated route, POST /requests/:id/repost, for the owner. It uses the existing repost checks, moved into repostRequest() with a conditional updateMany, and the token routes drafts/:token/repost and drafts/:token/edit are removed. (2) Treat the draft token as a DRAFT-only secret: publish sets draftTokenHash=null, findByToken returns 404 for anything that is not a DRAFT, and a data-only migration nulls the leftover hashes. The frontend stops writing mm_req_token_* and purges existing keys once. (3) Add owner tagging. On the server, findByToken takes the caller and returns 404 when a logged-in caller is not the draft's clientUserId, and patchDraft binds an anonymous draft to the logged-in caller. On the frontend, a new mm_local_owner key triggers a cleanup when a different user logs in. (4) Add lib/session-cleanup.ts, called on logout and on login as a different user. It clears the whole query cache, removes mm_draft_token and mm_req_token_*, resets the configurator store, sets studio accountDraft to null (after rehydration) and disconnects the socket. Logout asks for confirmation when an unpublished local request would be lost. (5) On the detail page, the repost button no longer depends on a token. When repostUsed is true, an explanation and a link to a new request replace it. No schema change, no new error codes, no business numbers changed.

decisions.question: Which error does publishing (or GET/PATCH) a draft that belongs to another user return: 403 FORBIDDEN or 404 DRAFT_TOKEN_INVALID?
decisions.chosen_default: 404 DRAFT_TOKEN_INVALID from findByToken, the same response as a dead token. It applies when draft.clientUserId is set, the caller is logged in and the caller is not the owner. Anonymous callers (null) keep access, so fill-as-guest still works.
decisions.why_safe: The playbook 'IMPACT endpoint nou' item 3 prescribes NOT_FOUND (not 403) for ownership in the service to avoid enumeration. The code already exists, with RO/EN copy in Requests.apiErrors that ReviewStep falls back to, and the wizard already recovers from a 404 token by creating a fresh draft.

decisions.question: Wipe the Studio's local content (scenes and pieces in mm_studio_v3) on logout?
decisions.chosen_default: Keep the scenes and pieces (current behaviour). Clear only accountDraft {id,name}, which points to the previous user's server draft.
decisions.why_safe: The audit doc lists this as an open PO question (docs/audit-2026-08-19/03-3d-studio.md Q2) and the finding says the accountDraft cleanup itself is not in question. Scenes hold no address or contact data. Keeping them is the non-destructive default.

decisions.question: C4-4 proposed_fix: allow one 'Modifică și republică' edit while EXPIRED and a 'Duplică cererea' action once repost is used?
decisions.chosen_default: Not implemented. The EXPIRED + repostUsed state shows an explanation and a link to /requests/new ('Începe o cerere nouă'), as WF1-12 proposes.
decisions.why_safe: Editing an EXPIRED request changes the edit-limit rules in docs/03 4.3 (3 edits before claim, 1 after, statuses allowed). Duplicating a request is a new product flow. Neither is decided in docs/03 or docs/07, so neither is added here.

decisions.question: Logout now wipes the unpublished configurator work in this browser, and its server draft cannot be resumed on login because the token is hash-only and drafts are not listed. How is the user warned?
decisions.chosen_default: When the persisted mm_configurator_v1 holds progress (rooms or details), logout first shows a native confirm with Common.logoutDiscardsLocalDraft (RO+EN). Cancel keeps the session. OK logs out and wipes. With no progress, there is no prompt.
decisions.why_safe: The approved plan mandates the wipe and flags that it 'needs clear wording'. A confirm is reversible, adds no business rule and matches the existing confirm() pattern on the request page. A later PO decision could make ciorne resumable from the account.

decisions.question: Should a draft created anonymously be bound to the first logged-in user who saves it (PATCH), before publish?
decisions.chosen_default: Yes. patchDraft sets clientUserId = caller when the draft has no owner and the caller is logged in. Publish already binds the owner (requests.service.ts publish: clientUserId: userId), per the decision 'fill as guest, login to publish'.
decisions.why_safe: It follows the existing binding semantics earlier in the flow and does not change who may publish. It closes the window in which a second account could pick up an anonymous draft that the first account had already edited while logged in.

decisions.question: The request.expired email always says 'O poți republica din pagina cererii', even on the second expiry after repostUsed=true.
decisions.chosen_default: Out of scope for this package and not changed here. Reported as a follow-up: carry repostUsed in the expiry outbox payload and switch the copy.

plan.brief:
E-client-3: implementer brief (Sprint 7: client publish and repost reliability)

GOAL: The client can repost an EXPIRED request from any logged-in device. After logout, nothing from the previous user stays in the browser. The draft token opens only a DRAFT, never a published request. A draft cannot be published by another account.

READ FIRST: Codex "BE requests", "FE auth", "FE configurator" and "IMPACT endpoint nou" (items 3, 7, 12, 13); skills nestjs-module, prisma-migration and ui-component. Invariants that apply: 3.6 (TanStack is the server state; no API data in Zustand) and 3.13 (sessions). docs/03 4.4 ("Repost permis o singura data") stays exactly as it is.

========== A. BACKEND (apps/backend/src/modules/requests) ==========

A1. requests.service.ts: findByToken with status guard and owner check
- Change the signature to `private async findByToken(token: string, callerId: string | null): Promise<RequestModel>` (required parameter, so every call site has to decide).
- After the existing `!request || request.deletedAt` check, add one condition that throws the same 404 DRAFT_TOKEN_INVALID:
  `request.status !== 'DRAFT' || (callerId !== null && request.clientUserId !== null && request.clientUserId !== callerId)`
  Comment: "// tokenul e secretul unei CIORNE: dupa publicare nu mai deschide nimic; un alt cont logat nu vede ciorna altcuiva (404, fara enumerare)".
- Call sites: getDraft(token, callerId), discardDraft(token, callerId), patchDraft(token, dto, callerId), publish (pass userId, which is already non-null at that point) and requireAttachmentEditable(token, callerId). Thread callerId through presignAttachment, confirmAttachment and removeAttachment.
- The existing `status !== 'DRAFT'` checks in discardDraft, patchDraft and publish become unreachable. Keep them as defence in depth.

A2. patchDraft: bind the owner
- Inside the existing tx.request.update data, add `...(callerId && !request.clientUserId ? { clientUserId: callerId } : {})`. This adds no extra query. Comment: "// ciorna anonima salvata de un user logat devine a lui (fill as guest, login to publish)".

A3. publish: clear the token
- In the existing tx.request.update data of publish, add `draftTokenHash: null,` next to `configuratorState: Prisma.DbNull`. Comment: "// tokenul de draft moare la publicare (SEC2-4); proprietarul lucreaza pe rutele autentificate :id". Add no other query inside the transaction.

A4. Repost for the owner (replaces repost(token))
- Delete `async repost(token)` and the token variant `async edit(token, dto)` (dead: a DRAFT cannot be edited and a published request no longer resolves by token).
- Add:
  ```ts
  // repost din contul proprietarului, de pe orice device (docs/03 4.4: o singura data, manual)
  async repostForClient(userId: string, id: string): Promise<RequestDto> {
    const request = await this.findOwnedRequest(userId, id);
    return this.repostRequest(request);
  }
  private async repostRequest(request: RequestModel): Promise<RequestDto> {
    if (request.status !== 'EXPIRED') throw new BadRequestException({ code: ERROR_CODES.REQUEST_NOT_EDITABLE, message: 'Only expired requests can be reposted' });
    if (request.repostUsed) throw new BadRequestException({ code: ERROR_CODES.REPOST_ALREADY_USED, message: 'Repost already used' });
    const now = new Date();
    const expiresAt = this.calendar.addWorkingDays(now, EXPIRATION_WORKING_DAYS);
    const reposted = await this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
      // updateMany conditionat: dublu-click / doua device-uri → un singur repost, un singur eveniment
      const res = await tx.request.updateMany({
        where: { id: request.id, status: 'EXPIRED', repostUsed: false, deletedAt: null },
        data: { status: 'IN_MARKETPLACE', repostUsed: true, publishedAt: now, expiresAt },
      });
      if (res.count !== 1) return false;
      await this.outbox.record(tx, `request.reposted:${request.id}`, 'request.status_changed', { requestId: request.id, status: 'IN_MARKETPLACE', reposted: true }, []);
      return true;
    }, REQUEST_WRITE_TX_OPTIONS);
    if (!reposted) throw new BadRequestException({ code: ERROR_CODES.REPOST_ALREADY_USED, message: 'Repost already used' });
    await this.scheduleExpiration(request.id, expiresAt);
    return this.toDto(request.id);
  }
  ```
  Keep the rest as it was: the same EXPIRATION_WORKING_DAYS constant (no new numbers), the same outbox key and the same scheduleExpiration.
- findOwnedRequest returns 404 NOT_FOUND or 403 FORBIDDEN. Keep it, for consistency with :id/edit.

A5. requests.controller.ts
- Remove `@Post('drafts/:token/edit')` and `@Post('drafts/:token/repost')`.
- Pass `@CurrentUser() user: AccessTokenPayload | undefined` and `user?.sub ?? null` into getDraft, patchDraft, discardDraft and the three drafts/:token/attachments routes. They stay @Public; OptionalJwtAuthGuard already sits on the controller.
- Add this after `:id/edit`:
  ```ts
  // Repost autentificat (proprietar, orice device) — inlocuieste ruta cu token (C4-4/WF1-12).
  @Roles(UserRole.CLIENT)
  @Post(':id/repost')
  repostById(@CurrentUser() user: AccessTokenPayload, @Param('id') id: string) {
    return this.requests.repostForClient(user.sub, id);
  }
  ```
  No @Idempotent: this is not money, and the conditional updateMany is the guard. docs/02 3.2 lists only claim, accept, quotes, webhook and credits. DeploymentStandbyGuard covers the POST automatically.

A6. Migration (data only). First run `ls apps/backend/prisma/migrations | tail -3`; the last one is 20260930190000_budget_range_from_estimate, and other Sprint 7 packages may add more, so pick a unique timestamp. Create `apps/backend/prisma/migrations/20260930200000_clear_published_draft_tokens/migration.sql`:
  ```sql
  -- E-client-3 (SEC2-4): tokenul de draft deschide doar o CIORNA. Hash-urile ramase pe
  -- cereri publicate/terminale sau pe ciorne sterse devin NULL. Doar date, schema neschimbata.
  -- Rollback: nimic de facut; imaginea anterioara citeste NULL (rutele cu token dau 404,
  -- inclusiv vechiul repost pe token). Hash-urile nu se pot reface (sha256 one-way).
  UPDATE "requests" SET "draft_token_hash" = NULL
  WHERE "draft_token_hash" IS NOT NULL AND ("status" <> 'DRAFT' OR "deleted_at" IS NOT NULL);
  ```

plan.summary: Plan for E-admin-platform-5 (Sprint 8, P1, findings SEC2-3, SEC1-21 and SEC2-11). (1) One client-IP resolver, used by the throttler, the audit log and the health endpoint. It trusts a configured edge header (X-Real-IP) only when TRUSTED_CLIENT_IP_HEADER is set and the peer is loopback, meaning the request came through the Next rewrite. The variable is unset by default, so nothing changes until an operator confirms that the Railway edge overwrites the header. (2) Throttler storage moves to Redis: a custom ThrottlerStorage (one Lua EVAL per request) with a timeout and a fallback to in-memory storage, switchable with THROTTLER_STORE=redis|memory. (3) A per-email failed-login lockout in Redis: 10 failures in 15 minutes, 5 for ADMIN accounts, then a 15-minute cooldown. Every email gets the same 429 LOGIN_COOLDOWN, whether or not the account exists and even with the correct password. The account owner gets one alert email and one audit row per lock. A successful login or password reset clears the counter. Redis errors fail open. (4) change-password is limited to 5/min per user through a route-level UserThrottlerGuard. (5) GET /auth/me becomes public with OptionalJwtAuthGuard. It returns 200 {user:null} when no access cookie, refresh cookie or Bearer header is present, and 401 only when session material exists. The frontend fetchMe turns user:null into a local ApiError 401, so all ~30 me.isError guards keep working without a /auth/refresh call. (6) verify-slot.mjs gets rate-limit checks: remaining must strictly decrease, a spoofed-header probe must stay in the same bucket, and health.client.scope must be public. No Prisma migration.

assumptions: Production chain is client -> Railway edge -> Caddy gateway (no trusted_proxies) -> app slot Next :3000 -> rewrite to 127.0.0.1:3001 Nest. Direct slot URLs are client -> edge -> Next -> Nest. In both paths the Railway edge is the first hop, and Caddy and Next pass X-Real-IP through unchanged, so X-Real-IP is trustworthy only if the edge overwrites it. This is unverified and gated behind an env var.

Locally the frontend uses NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/api/v1 through the Next rewrite to localhost:3001, so local traffic mirrors the prod proxy path. All local requests share ::1/127.0.0.1, and that is expected.

Throttler v6.5: a module-level getTracker overrides the guard's getTracker method, so the tracker goes in a ThrottlerGuard subclass registered as APP_GUARD, not in module options. ThrottlerModule is @Global, so the subclass and route-level guards can inject options and storage.

Global guard order stays DeploymentStandby -> Throttler -> Jwt -> Roles. The global throttler therefore cannot see req.user, so the per-user change-password limit is a route-level @UseGuards(UserThrottlerGuard), which runs after JwtAuthGuard.

Redis is ~150 ms per command from the slots until the approved EU migration (INFRA redis note), so Redis throttling adds one round trip per API request. It is kept to one EVAL, with a timeout and an in-memory fallback.

Invariant 3.13 (docs/02:99) requires per-IP limits of 5/min on login and 100/min global. This package keeps them, now keyed on the real client IP. The per-account lockout adds to the invariant and does not conflict with it. No decision in docs/07 covers lockout (the question is still open in docs/audit-2026-08-19/08-security-backend.md:83).
audit_logs.action is free text and the admin audit page shows it raw, so a new action string needs no i18n or migration.
Prod Redis version is unknown, so the design avoids Redis 7-only flags (PEXPIRE NX) and uses SET NX PX plus INCR in one MULTI instead.

decisions.question: Lockout thresholds for normal accounts: how many failures, over what window, and how long is the cooldown?
decisions.chosen_default: 10 failures in 15 minutes per normalized email, then a 15-minute cooldown. Constants live in auth.constants.ts (LOGIN_FAILURE_WINDOW_SEC=900, LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES=10, LOGIN_COOLDOWN_SEC=900).
decisions.why_safe: 10/15 min comes from the approved package steps. The 15-minute cooldown comes from the audit recommendation in docs/17-audit-prelansare-2026-08-19.md:78 and docs/audit-2026-08-19/08-security-backend.md:41 ('10 esecuri -> 15 min'). These are security constants, not prices or business numbers, and they are easy to tune.

decisions.question: What does 'stricter for admins' mean in practice? A lower threshold lets an attacker who already knows an email infer that it is an ADMIN account (lock after 5 attempts instead of 10).
decisions.chosen_default: LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES_ADMIN=5 in the same 15-minute window, with the same 15-minute cooldown, plus an audit row LOGIN_COOLDOWN_STARTED and an alert email on every lock. It is a single constant, so the PO can raise it to 10 to remove the role inference if preferred.
decisions.why_safe: It is only a security constant: no pricing, no policy lock-in, and trivially reversible. The inference needs the attacker to already hold the email and spend 5 attempts, and it is weighed against brute force on accounts that can confirm payments and block users.

decisions.question: Should the cooldown return the same INVALID_CREDENTIALS error or a dedicated cooldown message?
decisions.chosen_default: A dedicated 429 LOGIN_COOLDOWN (details.retryAfterSec plus a Retry-After header). It is returned identically for existing and non-existing emails and even when the password is correct. The attempt that reaches the threshold already returns LOGIN_COOLDOWN. It is checked before the DB lookup and bcrypt.
decisions.why_safe: It satisfies both the done_when ('trigger a cooldown message') and the acceptance ('same error returned either way'), meaning uniform across account existence. It keeps the ACCOUNT_BLOCKED-only-after-correct-password rule from the BE auth note.

decisions.question: Which forwarded header carries the real client IP in production, and has the Railway edge been confirmed to overwrite it (the package's do_first)?
decisions.chosen_default: The code supports TRUSTED_CLIENT_IP_HEADER (expected x-real-ip). It is unset by default, which keeps today's req.ip behaviour. 'x-forwarded-for' is rejected by config validation. The header is honoured only when the socket peer is loopback. Production boot logs a warning while it is unset. The operator runs the spoof test (verify-slot's new spoof probe, or a curl with X-Real-IP: 203.0.113.77 against the public health URL comparing x-ratelimit-remaining) and then sets the variable on both app-blue and app-green.
decisions.why_safe: A wrong trusted header would let attackers pick their bucket, so the rollout is gated on a production observation that the implementer must not make. Both old and new slots boot with or without the variable, so rollback stays compatible.

decisions.question: Throttler in Redis adds about 150 ms per API request while Redis is still in another region. Accept that now, or keep in-memory storage on prod until the EU migration?
decisions.chosen_default: THROTTLER_STORE defaults to 'redis', with a 1000 ms command timeout and a per-process in-memory fallback on error or timeout. The PO or operator may set THROTTLER_STORE=memory on both slots until green-redis in EU West is live. The login lockout always uses Redis, since it only runs on login.
decisions.why_safe: It is a runtime switch and does not change behaviour contracts. The fallback avoids 5xx or an open door when Redis is slow or down, and the per-IP limits hold either way.

decisions.question: Does a successful password reset clear the lockout, and does a correct password during cooldown get through?
decisions.chosen_default: resetPassword clears login-fail and login-lock for that user's email, because the reset link proves control of the address. A correct password during cooldown is still refused with LOGIN_COOLDOWN, or the lock would not stop guessing. A successful login deletes the failure counter.
decisions.why_safe: It is standard lockout semantics with no business policy. The legitimate user always has a self-service way out (reset) and the lock expires on its own.

decisions.question: Contract of GET /auth/me for anonymous visitors (SEC2-11).
decisions.chosen_default: It returns 200 {user:null} only when no mm_access cookie, no mm_refresh cookie and no Authorization header is present. Otherwise it returns 401 as today, so the frontend refreshes on a real expiry. The frontend fetchMe throws a local ApiError('UNAUTHORIZED', 401) on user:null, so every existing me.isError redirect guard keeps its behaviour without touching ~30 pages.
decisions.why_safe: It follows the finding's proposed fix. REFRESH_COOKIE_PATH=/api/v1/auth covers /auth/me, so the server can tell 'no session' from 'expired'. The 401 path for real sessions is unchanged.

plan.summary: Plan for E-company-3, Sprint 8, "Close the free-refund loopholes and limit who sees client contact data". There is one blocking PO question. The decisions are FINAL: W1 (docs/03 4.2) reveals contacts at claim, and I18 gives a full refund within 30 minutes. Changing when contacts show, or whether the 30-minute refund survives a reveal, reopens them. So the sprint does not choose. It ships a system_settings switch, claim_contact_reveal_policy, whose default ON_CLAIM keeps today's behaviour. The other value, AFTER_GRACE, hides contacts during the 30-minute refund window. A monthly cap and "reveal cancels refund" are not built, because they would invent a policy. The approved package steps are implemented in full. (1) CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H needs a firm chat message or clarification that is at least 48h old and unanswered; a clarification answer counts as client activity. (2) REQUEST_MODIFIED_POST_CLAIM stays valid only until the firm sends an offer after the edit. This window comes from 4.3 and uses no invented number. (3) EMPLOYEE_MANAGED members get client contacts and the full address only on slots they claimed or are assigned to. (4) The cutoff for completed claims is a setting, completed_claim_contact_retention_days, with default 0 (off), because the warranty is free text and gives no duration. (5) GET /quotes/by-claim returns a REDACTED summary for non-occupying slots and a TOMBSTONE for deleted requests. Neither mode presigns files or returns answers, scenes or contacts. No schema change is needed. A data-only migration adds the two settings rows.

backend: claims (withdrawals.service autoReasonEligibility + signal loader, claims.constants)

assumptions: The approved package steps and acceptance (48h needs firm outreach, time-limited REQUEST_MODIFIED_POST_CLAIM, managed-employee restriction, redacted or tombstone context) carry PO approval. The one open PO item is the package's decision_needed (reveal timing, grace refund after reveal, monthly cap) plus the retention value.
W1 (docs/03 4.2) and I18 (docs/07) stay in force by default: every new switch defaults to today's behaviour, and nothing is written into docs/07.

'Firm outreach' means a chat message in the claim thread from anyone other than request.client_user_id, or a clarification the firm created. 'Client activity' means chat_threads.last_client_message_at or clarification_requests.answered_at. Sending an offer is not outreach, as the acceptance says: in-app message or clarification.
Only one clarification can be PENDING at a time (CLARIFICATION_ALREADY_PENDING), so the answered_at of the newest clarification is the latest clarification answer.

Post-claim edits happen only before any offer on the request (OFFER_LOCKED_STATUSES in requests.service), so any quote version of this slot sent after last_edit_at means the firm accepted the modified request.

OWNER, MANAGER and EMPLOYEE_TRUSTED keep full contact access on any occupying slot. EMPLOYEE_MANAGED sees contacts only where claimed_by_user_id or assigned_to_user_id equals the caller. Managed staff never claim (4.7), so in practice this means assigned_to.
The redacted summary keeps city and county, because both are public in the marketplace list before a claim. The tombstone drops them. Both keep the title, because GET /claims/mine already shows it.
The anchor for the retention cutoff is requests.delivered_at, falling back to claim_slots.updated_at. It is only used when completed_claim_contact_retention_days > 0.

No schema column is added: firm outreach is computed with indexed reads (messages.chat_thread_id, clarification_requests.claim_slot_id). The 'GET must be safe on standby' rule forbids writing a contact_revealed_at from the by-claim GET anyway.
Old and new images read the same shape: the new DTO fields are additive and the FE treats a missing visibility as FULL.

decisions.question: When should a firm see the client's contacts, and does revealing them affect the 30-minute free refund? Options: (a) contacts only after the 30-minute grace window; (b) contacts only after the firm's first chat message or offer; (c) keep reveal at claim but make the grace refund unavailable once contacts were seen; (d) cap grace refunds per firm per 30 days (what cap, and what happens above it?).
decisions.chosen_default: Keep W1 + I18 exactly as now. Add the setting claim_contact_reveal_policy with values 'ON_CLAIM' (default, today's behaviour) and 'AFTER_GRACE' (contacts and full address hidden until claim_slots.created_at + VOLUNTARY_WITHDRAWAL_GRACE_MS, FE shows when they appear). Admin can switch it from Admin > Settings with no deploy. (b), (c) and (d) are not built: (b) needs (c) to close the loophole, and (c) and (d) need a PO-defined consequence (consume? penalty?) that docs do not give. Log it as DECIZIE NECESARA in CHANGELOG and docs/04, not docs/07.
decisions.why_safe: No FINAL decision changes until the PO flips the switch. The mechanism for the most likely fix (a) is ready, and reuses the existing 30-minute constant, so no new number is invented.

decisions.question: CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H: must the firm have messaged the client (and been ignored for 48h), rather than 48h simply passing since the claim?
decisions.chosen_default: Implement as the approved acceptance says. The reason is eligible only when there is firm outreach (last firm chat message or clarification) that is at least 48h old, with no client message or clarification answer after it. eligibleFrom = outreach + 48h. Update the docs/03 4.15 row wording, citing E-company-3.
decisions.why_safe: It narrows an automatic refund that docs/03 and D5 say must be 'validated' (it proves the client is unresponsive). It changes no price or duration (48h stays), and it is the explicit acceptance criterion of the approved package.

decisions.question: REQUEST_MODIFIED_POST_CLAIM: how long after the edit may a firm still withdraw with a refund?
decisions.chosen_default: Eligible only if last_edit_at > claim_slots.created_at AND no quote version of this slot (quote status not DRAFT) has sent_at > last_edit_at. The window closes when the firm sends an offer on the modified request. No hour limit is added. Ask the PO whether a fixed hour limit is also wanted.
decisions.why_safe: The bound follows from 4.3 (a post-claim edit happens only before offers) and invents no duration. Offering on the new version shows the firm accepted the change.

decisions.question: Should the 48h auto-refund still be allowed after the firm has sent an offer (slot OFFER_SENT)? Pay-to-play consumes the credits of losing bidders.
decisions.chosen_default: Leave it unchanged. OFFER_SENT slots can still use CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H, but they now also need the firm-outreach condition.
decisions.why_safe: It does not change settlement policy without a decision. The new outreach requirement already makes it harder to abuse.

decisions.question: Who inside a firm may read client contacts and the full address on an occupying claim?
decisions.chosen_default: OWNER/MANAGER/EMPLOYEE_TRUSTED: yes. EMPLOYEE_MANAGED: only on slots where they are claimed_by or assigned_to. Otherwise client = null, detail.addressText = '', consultation invite locationAddress = '', clientHiddenReason = 'NOT_ASSIGNED_TO_YOU'.
decisions.why_safe: W1 settles firm versus other firms and says nothing about roles. This is least privilege and matches 4.7/D6 (managed staff work on assigned_to). It is also an approved package step. It removes read access only and moves no credits.

decisions.question: How long after completion may non-managers still see a client's contacts (the 'warranty window')?
decisions.chosen_default: Add the setting completed_claim_contact_retention_days, default 0 = no cutoff (today's behaviour). When it is > 0, COMPLETED slots whose delivered_at (fallback: slot updated_at) is older than N days hide contacts from everyone except OWNER/MANAGER (reason RETENTION_EXPIRED). Admin validator: integer 0..3650.
decisions.why_safe: quote_versions.warranty is free text, so there is no duration to derive, and the sprint invents none. The mechanism ships switched off.

decisions.question: What may a firm see on a claim that is no longer occupying (withdrawn, SLA-expired, lost, auto-cancelled, project cancelled, offer expired), or whose request was deleted?
decisions.chosen_default: docs/03 4.2: contacts go when a claim is withdrawn or cancelled, and project materials and 3D scenes follow project-detail authorization, which marketplace limits to claimable, non-deleted requests. REDACTED keeps the title, city, county, statuses, top-level room ids and types (to label own per-room prices), the firm's latest own quote including WITHDRAWN (with consultation locationAddress blanked), projectCase, assignment names and claimCostCredits. Everything else is emptied, and uploads.listForEntity is never called. TOMBSTONE (request.deleted_at set) is REDACTED without city, county, rooms or projectCase.
decisions.why_safe: It follows the existing rule in docs/03 4.2 and removes read access only.

decisions.question: The done_when asks for 'Decisions log shows the chosen contact and refund rule'.
decisions.chosen_default: Do not edit docs/07. Record the open question as DECIZIE NECESARA in CHANGELOG.md and in the docs/04 5.4 note next to the new setting. The PO writes the docs/07 entry once they decide; after that, only the setting value changes.
decisions.why_safe: The rules forbid touching FINAL decisions, and an entry written before the PO decides would be invented.

feat(security): sprint 8 abuse and fraud hardening (E-admin-platform-5, E-company-3)

- Client-IP resolver (trusted edge header only with TRUSTED_CLIENT_IP_HEADER and a loopback peer) shared by throttler, audit and health; throttler storage in Redis with an in-memory fallback (THROTTLER_STORE)
- Per-email login lockout: 10 failures in 15 min (5 for ADMIN) -> 429 LOGIN_COOLDOWN, the same whether or not the account exists; alert email and LOGIN_COOLDOWN_STARTED audit row; change-password limited to 5/min per user
- GET /auth/me returns 200 {user:null} to anonymous visitors (no /auth/refresh storm); verify-slot checks rate limits and spoofing
- Withdrawals: CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H requires firm outreach unanswered for 48h+; REQUEST_MODIFIED_POST_CLAIM refunds only until an offer is sent on the edited request
- by-claim context: FULL/REDACTED/TOMBSTONE; EMPLOYEE_MANAGED sees contacts only on own or assigned claims; limited modes presign no request files
- Data-only migration 20260930210000_claim_contact_access_settings (ON_CLAIM / 0, keeps W1 + I18); docs 03/04/08, ERROR_CODES, CHANGELOG

plan.summary:
Plan for E-admin-platform-25 (Sprint 19, "Count all Romanian holidays in firm deadlines"). All four findings (DATA1-11, A1-21, R2-TESTS-12, VQ4-3) are in scope and none is skipped.

1. **Fixed holidays.** BusinessCalendarService drops its hand-written FIXED_HOLIDAYS list (which misses 6 and 7 January) and takes fixed public holidays from the date-holidays library (Romania, version 3.37.0; verified to include 1-2, 6, 7 and 24 January). This is what Decision 6 and invariant 3.3 require.
2. **Movable holidays.** Easter and Pentecost stay in the business_calendar_holidays table, as the decision says. A new idempotent data migration inserts the Good Friday, Easter Monday and Whit Monday dates for 2025-2030 (verified against the library). The library is used only to check coverage: the server logs a warning and the admin page shows a banner when next year's dates are missing.
3. **Admin calendar.** A new admin CRUD at /admin/calendar (list, add, edit, delete) plus a read-only deadline calculator. Each change reloads the local cache and publishes a Redis message so the other blue/green slot reloads too. A 10-minute periodic reload is a safety net if a message is missed.
4. **Sizing weights.** A new /admin/sizing editor for the weights (0..100, existing rows only) with a preview. The preview re-scores the last 200 published requests with the current and proposed weights and shows the S/M/L distribution and credit-cost impact. The UI only allows saving after a preview.
5. **Tests.** A table-driven calendar spec covers the full statutory holiday list, the 5 January 2026 claim (deadline 12 January), movable dates, winter time and DST-change days, bridge days, and a guard that fails when next year has no movable holidays.

No schema change is needed, only the data migration.
modules: modules/admin (new AdminCalendarController/Service, new AdminSizingController/Service, DTOs, module wiring)
modules/sizing (extract pure computeSizing function reused by preview)
apps/frontend admin (hooks/use-admin.ts, /admin/calendar page, /admin/sizing page, layout NAV, ro/en messages)
tables: business_calendar_holidays (R/W: data migration inserts 2025-2030 movable rows; admin CRUD; no DDL change)
project_sizing_config (R/W: admin weight edits; no DDL change)
project_size_thresholds (R only, preview classification)
requests + request_rooms (R only, preview sample of last 200 published requests)
audit_logs (W via AuditInterceptor: CALENDAR_HOLIDAY_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED, SIZING_WEIGHTS_UPDATED)
files: E:/CozyFableObsidian/CozyFableCodex/10 Module BE/INFRA calendar.md, BE admin.md, BE sizing.md; 20 Frontend/FE admin.md (Codex update after delivery)
assumptions: Decision 6 is read as: date-holidays supplies the FIXED public holidays only. Rules matching /orthodox|easter/ are excluded at runtime. Movable holidays (Good Friday, Easter Monday, Whit Monday) keep coming ONLY from business_calendar_holidays. The library's orthodox dates are used only as a reference: for the coverage warning and to cross-check the migration in tests.

date-holidays 3.37.0, country RO, type 'public' gives exactly the current list plus 6 and 7 January. New Year is one rule with a 2-day duration ('01-01 P2DT'), so the expansion must follow start/end. This was probed in a scratch install on 2026-09-30. The library also reports 6-7 January before 2024, which is irrelevant because no deadline is computed in the past.

No schema change: the existing columns (date, name, is_working_day, created_at) cover the CRUD, so bridge days and forced working days share the table with the movable rows. Who changed what is recorded in audit_logs.

Deadlines already stored in the DB (sla_deadline_at, expires_at, withdraw windows) and BullMQ jobs already scheduled are NOT recalculated. A calendar change affects only new calculations, per invariant 3.3 (materialized at claim).

Both blue/green slots share Redis, so Redis pub/sub on channel 'calendar:holidays:changed' reaches the standby slot. The standby slot only reloads its cache (a read), which DeploymentStandbyGuard allows. Admin mutations are POST/PATCH/DELETE, so they run only on the active slot.
Weight edits take effect immediately: SizingService has no cache and reads project_sizing_config on every compute. Claims keep their snapshot (D1), so only requests published or edited later change.

The preview recomputes both the 'current' and the 'proposed' columns from request_rooms answers via collectScoreEntries. Rooms without answers (legacy) or with unregistered flow versions are counted as skipped. Stored size_score is not used, because it may predate earlier weight edits.
Local DB currently has 12 movable rows (2025-2028), 65 sizing rows and 37 published requests. admin@demo.ro has no 2FA.

decisions.question: Where do fixed vs movable Romanian holidays come from (hand list, date-holidays, or DB)?
decisions.chosen_default: Hybrid per docs/07 Decision 6 and docs/02 invariant 3.3. Fixed holidays come from date-holidays('RO'), type public, with orthodox/easter rules excluded. Movable holidays and admin overrides come from business_calendar_holidays. The overrides keep priority and stay bidirectional.
decisions.why_safe: It is exactly the FINAL decision. Keeping Easter in the DB honours the rationale that libraries may compute Orthodox Easter wrongly; the library is only a cross-check.

decisions.question: When the calendar changes, should existing SLA/expiry deadlines be recalculated?
decisions.chosen_default: No. Only new calculations use the new calendar. The admin page says so explicitly.
decisions.why_safe: Invariant 3.3 says the SLA is materialized at claim time and changes only through the clarification worker. Recalculating would silently move penalties and expiries already communicated to firms and clients.

decisions.question: How do both live slots pick up an admin calendar change without a restart?
decisions.chosen_default: CalendarSyncService.notifyChanged(): refresh the local cache, then PUBLISH on the Redis channel 'calendar:holidays:changed'. Every process subscribes through REDIS_CLIENT.duplicate() and reloads on each message. A 10-minute unref'd setInterval reload is the safety net. Every failure path only logs a warning (safeErrorSummary).
decisions.why_safe: It is a purely technical mechanism. It is read-only on the standby slot, needs no new infrastructure (Redis is already shared by both slots), and the periodic reload bounds staleness if a message is lost.

decisions.question: How far ahead are movable holidays seeded, and how does the system warn when they run out?
decisions.chosen_default: An idempotent data migration inserts 2025-2030, using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (date) DO NOTHING, which never overwrites admin edits. Any missing movable dates for next year trigger a warn log once per process per year. GET /admin/calendar also returns a coverage block that the admin page shows as an amber banner. A jest guard fails when MOVABLE_HOLIDAYS has no rows for next year (currentYear + 1). No email or outbox notification is added.
decisions.why_safe: The rows are data, not policy; the dates match date-holidays orthodox rules and are checked in a test. An outbox alert would need a new event type, which is out of scope.

decisions.question: May admins edit sizing weights at runtime, given that they change the client estimate and the claim credit cost (1 credit = 1,000 RON of base score)?
decisions.chosen_default: Yes, per D1 ('Permite ajustare fara deploy') and docs/03 4.5 ('Punctele se ajustează ulterior din Admin Settings'). Only existing rows can be edited (no new key/option). The formula and all numbers stay the same. Integer weights 0..100 as a validation cap. Save is audited (SIZING_WEIGHTS_UPDATED). The UI shows the credit-cost impact in a mandatory preview and asks for confirmation. seed.ts stops overwriting weights (update: {}) so admin edits survive a re-seed.
decisions.why_safe: Snapshots on claim_slots protect claims already made. The preview makes the pricing impact visible before saving. No price or business number changes in code.

decisions.question: Which dates can an admin add to the calendar?
decisions.chosen_default: From today (Bucharest) up to 31 Dec of currentYear+5. The date must be a real calendar date; one row per date (the unique index maps to 409 CALENDAR_DATE_EXISTS). Delete and edit work on any row, including migration rows, so an admin can fix a wrong date.
decisions.why_safe: Past dates have no effect because deadlines are materialized, so blocking them avoids confusion. Editing or deleting stays possible for corrections, and everything is audited.

decisions.question: Should the public firm-rules page (Legal.firmRules) mention that government bridge days are also non-working days?
decisions.chosen_default: Leave the text unchanged. It already says working days exclude weekends and legal holidays. No Legal.* copy is edited in this package.
decisions.why_safe: IMPACT text UI says Legal.* texts change only with PO agreement. The current text is not wrong for fixed or movable holidays.

==== 3. calendar-sync.service.ts (NEW) + calendar.module.ts ====
```ts
export const CALENDAR_CHANNEL = 'calendar:holidays:changed';
const RELOAD_MS = 10 * 60_000;
@Injectable()
export class CalendarSyncService implements OnModuleInit, OnModuleDestroy {
  constructor(private readonly calendar: BusinessCalendarService, @Inject(REDIS_CLIENT) private readonly redis: Redis) {}
  onModuleInit(): void {
    // ambele sloturi blue/green: doar reincarcare cache (citire) - permis si pe standby
    this.timer = setInterval(() => void this.reload('interval'), RELOAD_MS); this.timer.unref?.();
    this.sub = this.redis.duplicate();
    this.sub.on('message', (ch) => { if (ch === CALENDAR_CHANNEL) void this.reload('pubsub'); });
    void this.sub.subscribe(CALENDAR_CHANNEL).catch((e) => this.logger.warn(`calendar subscribe failed: ${safeErrorSummary(e)}`));
  }
  async onModuleDestroy() { clearInterval(this.timer); await this.sub?.quit().catch(() => undefined); }
  // apelat de admin dupa orice modificare: cache local imediat + celelalte procese prin Redis
  async notifyChanged(): Promise<void> { await this.calendar.refresh(); await this.redis.publish(CALENDAR_CHANNEL, String(Date.now())).catch((e) => this.logger.warn(...safeErrorSummary(e))); }
  private async reload(src) { await this.calendar.refresh().catch((e) => this.logger.warn(`calendar reload (${src}) failed: ${safeErrorSummary(e)}`)); }
}
```
- Do not await `subscribe` in `onModuleInit`, so boot does not block when Redis is down.
- `REDIS_CLIENT` comes from infra/redis/redis.module (global).
- CalendarModule: `providers: [BusinessCalendarService, CalendarSyncService]`, `exports: [BusinessCalendarService, CalendarSyncService]`.

plan.summary: Plan for E-admin-platform-44 (Sprint 19, P2, about 3 days). The package adds three timed nudges and a "De făcut acum" card on both dashboards. (1) The client gets a reminder when a request has had no claim for 3 working days (docs/03 4.4). (2) OWNER/MANAGER get a warning at +30 min when a claim is still unassigned (docs/03 4.9 and docs/07 D2; the code comment calling it an open PO decision is stale). (3) The assignee and OWNER/MANAGER get sla.expiring_soon 24 h before sla_deadline_at (docs/02 3.5 minimum event; 24 h comes from the approved package). Each nudge is a delayed BullMQ job on the EXISTING domain queue under a new job name: request-expiration 'remind-expiry', claim-assign 'warn-assign', sla-breach 'warn-sla'. Reusing the queues means no constructor changes and no ripple into the positional-constructor specs. Job ids are deterministic and include the deadline. Each nudge also gets a reconciliation sweep branch, deduplicated on a deterministic outbox eventKey, and a targeted outbox event with a RO/EN email template, bell entry and socket invalidation. The dashboards get an `actions` array on the existing dashboard-stats endpoints (no new endpoint), rendered by a new TodoNowCard with one-click links. There is no Prisma schema change and no migration. One additive calendar helper is needed (workingDateBefore). The package overlaps heavily with sibling package E-company-13 (same +30 min and SLA-24 h jobs), so the brief tells the implementer to check which package landed first and not build the warnings twice.

assumptions: No Prisma schema change is needed. Event types are free-text strings in domain_event_outbox.event_type and notifications.type. Every deadline is already materialized (requests.expires_at, claim_slots.assign_deadline_at, claim_slots.sla_deadline_at), so the sweep can rebuild every reminder from columns.

Reusing the three existing queues with new job names follows the bullmq-worker skill ('one queue per domain'). It avoids constructor changes in ReconciliationProcessor, QuotesService, ClaimsService and RequestsService, which the specs build positionally. The only risk is that a processor sees a job name it does not know, so each processor branches on job.name FIRST and keeps the old path as the default.
Warning jobs never move money or change state. They read state, check it, and write one outbox row. They do not take FOR UPDATE locks and do not need Serializable isolation.

The request reminder runs at 09:00 Europe/Bucharest on the first of the last 2 working days before expires_at (D4 of a 5-working-day clock). At that point 3 full working days have passed (docs/03 4.4) and 2 remain. 09:00 mirrors the existing DELIVERY_REMINDER_HOUR convention. The reminder is derived from expires_at, not published_at, so re-publish clocks (D-v6-13, withdrawals, auto-cancel) are covered automatically.
'Still unclaimed' means status IN_MARKETPLACE and deleted_at IS NULL. CLAIMED_PARTIAL and later statuses never expire, so they never get a reminder.

The SLA warning goes out once per sla_deadline_at value (eventKey includes the deadline in ms). A clarification that moves the deadline can therefore produce a second warning for the new deadline. Paused claims (sla_paused_at set) are skipped. The grace-start reminder is out of scope here; it belongs to E-company-13 step 4.
Title and company name are rehydrated by the outbox dispatcher from requestId/companyId, so payloads carry only ids, deadlines and clientUserId (IMPACT eveniment nou step 5).

E-admin-platform-25 (same sprint) rewrites the calendar internals. The new workingDateBefore uses only the private isWorkingDay() and a new private subtractCalendarDay(), so it survives that rewrite. If package 25 lands first, add the method to its new structure.
The demo client ana.popescu@demo.ro and the owner owner.a@demo.ro have email_verified_at set and email notifications enabled. Check this in the DB before the Mailpit checks.

decisions.question: Should the client get a reminder before a request expires, and when?
decisions.chosen_default: Yes, per docs/03 4.4 ('Reminder la clientul cererii la 3 zile lucrătoare'). Send at 09:00 Bucharest on the first of the last 2 working days before expires_at, only while the request is IN_MARKETPLACE and not deleted.
decisions.why_safe: The docs already set the rule. The 09:00 hour is only a delivery-time detail that copies the existing delivery-reminder convention. It is a notification only, with no state or money change.

decisions.question: Is the +30 min unassigned-claim warning still an open PO decision, as claims.constants.ts says?
decisions.chosen_default: No. docs/03 4.9 and docs/07 D2 (Impact: 'warning +30 min') decide it. Implement it and replace the stale comment. docs/07 is not edited.
decisions.why_safe: It follows a FINAL decision and does not reopen anything.

decisions.question: How long before the SLA deadline is sla.expiring_soon sent?
decisions.chosen_default: 24 h wall-clock before sla_deadline_at, as the PO-approved package states (steps and acceptance). Stored as the shared constant SLA_WARNING_BEFORE_HOURS = 24, which the backend and the dashboard both use. docs/03 4.11 gets a one-line implementation note.
decisions.why_safe: The number comes from the approved package, not an invention. It only triggers a notification and a dashboard highlight. It does not change SLA duration, grace, credits or penalties. Short clocks are wall-clock per docs/07 D-v6-9.

decisions.question: Who receives the assign warning and the SLA warning?
decisions.chosen_default: Assign warning: OWNER/MANAGER members plus claimed_by_user_id. SLA warning: assigned_to_user_id (or claimed_by_user_id when unassigned) plus OWNER/MANAGER. The target set is deduplicated.
decisions.why_safe: These are the people who can act (only OWNER/MANAGER can assign), which matches the sibling package E-company-13 finding F3-5. It is a notification only; the auto-cancel and breach processors keep notifying all members as before.

decisions.question: Which items does each role see in the firm 'De făcut acum' card?
decisions.chosen_default: OWNER/MANAGER see all unassigned ACTIVE claims plus every ACTIVE, non-paused claim with SLA under 24 h (including claims still in grace). EMPLOYEE_* roles see no unassigned list (they cannot assign) and only SLA items assigned to them, or claimed by them while unassigned.
decisions.why_safe: It only filters an actionable list. All members can already see the whole claims list (/claims/mine), so no data is hidden or exposed differently.

decisions.question: Should the three nudges also send email?
decisions.chosen_default: Yes. All three event types are added to EMAILED_EVENTS, with RO/EN templates escaped via esc(). They honour email_notifications_enabled, the unsubscribe link and email_verified_at like every other event.
decisions.why_safe: The approved acceptance requires 'a targeted outbox event with an email template'. The opt-out path is unchanged.

decisions.question: Is the +30 min assignment warning an open PO decision (old comment in claims.constants said so)?
decisions.chosen_default: Implemented (already in the tree): D2 Impact 'warning +30 min' (docs/07:85) and 4.9 'Warning la +30 min' (docs/03). Keep as is.
decisions.why_safe: The FINAL decision D2 explicitly requires it; D-v6-9 says it is a wall-clock clock.

decisions.question: When should the SLA reminders fire?
decisions.chosen_default: 24h before sla_deadline_at (SLA_WARNING_BEFORE_HOURS, already recorded in docs/03 4.11 note) plus a second reminder at sla_deadline_at (start of the 12h grace). The approved package step 4 asks for both. No new duration is introduced: the grace start equals the existing deadline, and the grace length is the existing SLA_GRACE_MS (docs/03 4.11).
decisions.why_safe: Notification only: no credits, penalties or state change. It is skipped for paused/closed/moved deadlines and dedupes on eventKey.

decisions.question: Who receives the reminders?
decisions.chosen_default: The existing claimAlertTargets helper: OWNER/MANAGER plus the claimer. The assign warning excludes the assignee because there is none. The SLA warnings include the assignee. Only current members.
decisions.why_safe: Matches the approved step 4 ('assignee and OWNER/MANAGER') and the docs/03 4.9/4.11 notes already written by E-admin-platform-44.

decisions.why_safe: Technical choice with no business policy. It keeps invariant 3.5 (sla.expiring_soon is the named event), and the bell/email/socket already handle the type.

  export function slaGraceWarningJobOptions(claimSlotId: string, slaDeadlineAt: Date) {
    return { delay: Math.max(0, slaDeadlineAt.getTime() - Date.now()),
             jobId: `sla-grace-warn-${claimSlotId}-${slaDeadlineAt.getTime()}`,
             removeOnComplete: true as const, removeOnFail: 1000 };
  }

On this Windows host, localhost connections to the Docker ports are flaky: my own bullmq script got ECONNRESET on 'localhost' and worked on 127.0.0.1. The /admin/calendar (GET, POST, PATCH/DELETE :id, GET check) and /admin/sizing (GET weights, POST preview, PUT weights) controllers use @Roles(ADMIN). Global APP_GUARDs (JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard, ClientIpThrottlerGuard in auth.module.ts, DeploymentStandbyGuard in app.module.ts) apply to them. :id goes through ParseUUIDPipe. Dashboard `actions` ride on the existing dashboard-stats routes, scoped by clientUserId, or by companyId plus role (EMPLOYEE_* roles see only their own SLA claims).

2. Input validation: PASS. The class-validator DTOs cover date YYYY-MM-DD plus a real-date and horizon check in the service, name 2..120, year 2024..2100, workingDays 1..30, weights int 0..100, and at most 200 changes. Duplicate ids give 400 and unknown ids give 404.

3. Idempotency on money mutations: N/A (PASS). The sprint adds no money, claim or accept mutation. The warning jobs only write outbox rows, use deterministic jobIds and eventKeys, and move no credits or penalties (asserted in jest). PUT weights is idempotent by nature.

4. Audit on critical ops: FAIL, now fixed. SIZING_WEIGHTS_UPDATED stored only the new weight, and these weights change the claim credit cost, so a change could not be reverted from the audit log. The CALENDAR_HOLIDAY_* rows correctly store date and isWorkingDay without the free-text name.

5. PII in logs and payloads: PASS. The new logs carry only ids and safeErrorSummary. Outbox payloads carry ids and deadlines, and title and company name are rehydrated at delivery. Emails escape values with esc(). Alert targets used to include removed ex-members; the E-admin-platform-44 verifier already fixed this in claimAlertTargets (current members only).

7. Error format: PASS. The new CALENDAR_DATE_EXISTS (409) is in packages/shared error-codes.ts and docs/ERROR_CODES.md, and every other error uses the single error format.
8. Soft-delete filters: PASS. The dashboard actions and the reminder processors filter requests on deletedAt: null, and the warn-sla-grace job does nothing for a deleted or settled request.
9. Cookies/CORS: PASS (unchanged).

10. i18n parity: PASS. ro 3445 = en 3445 keys, no key missing on either side, 0 occurrences of 'atelier'. ro.json and en.json still show as whole-file rewrites (HEAD is CRLF, the working tree is LF); this is diff noise only, not a security issue.

plan.summary: Plan for E-admin-platform-45 (Sprint 20, finding F2-16). A new shared contact detector finds RO and international phone numbers, emails (including obfuscated forms like [at]/arond), URLs and bare domains, @handles and messenger-app mentions. It is run at publish and edit on the title, the "Mesaj pentru firme" description and the free-text answers (text steps plus pieces[].name/description). Default behaviour is MASK, stored in a new system_settings key `pre_claim_contact_text_policy` (MASK|BLOCK). In MASK mode the stored text stays as typed. Any view that reaches a firm without contact access replaces matches with a `⟦contact⟧` token, which the frontend renders as a localized chip. That covers the marketplace list and detail (title, description, text/pieces answers, item name/description, Studio scene names) and the by-claim detail when `access.clientVisible=false` (EMPLOYEE_MANAGED not assigned, AFTER_GRACE). In BLOCK mode publish/edit returns 400 `REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO_IN_TEXT` with per-field details. A manual title containing contact data is always replaced by the auto-generated title. Every hit goes into a new table `request_contact_detections` with a redacted excerpt; in MASK mode the write is one createMany inside the existing transaction, only when there are hits. Admins read the list at GET /admin/contact-detections and on a new admin page. The client sees a non-blocking hint as soon as they type a phone or email. Migration is additive: one table plus one settings row.
modules: apps/backend admin (new contact-detections controller/service, setting validation)
tables: request_contact_detections (NEW)
system_settings (new key pre_claim_contact_text_policy)
requests (read only; stored text unchanged)
request_rooms / request_items (read only)
request_studio_scenes (read only, name masked at read)
assumptions: docs/03 §4.2 (contacts visible only to a firm with an occupying claim, checked in the API) covers free text too. So hiding contact data typed into free text from firms without contact access applies the existing rule; it is not a new policy. Only 'block vs mask' is a new product choice.

Stored request text is never rewritten: the client keeps seeing exactly what they typed, and masking happens only when building firm-facing DTOs. Legacy published requests are therefore covered with no backfill.

Firm-facing free text = title, description, answers of 'text' steps, pieces[].name/description, request_items.name/description (derived from those answers) and top-level Studio scene names. House/room labels inside request_studio_scenes.data are not deep-masked in this package (max 60-char labels, strict FE parser); logged as a follow-up.
The UI never sends a manual title (details-step shows an auto-title preview). A manual title comes only from direct API calls, so replacing it with the server auto-title is safe.
A messenger mention with no contact data ('prefer WhatsApp') leaks nothing. It is logged as FLAGGED and never masked or blocked.

Spelled-out digits ('zero sapte doi doi...'), numbers split across fields and images/attachments are out of scope. The detector targets common written formats, and the admin log shows abuse patterns for later tuning.

Firm notifications/emails carry only requestTitle, which is auto-generated from here on. The firm 'my claims' list titles for legacy manual titles are not re-masked (very low risk, logged as follow-up).

Parallel Sprint 20 packages may add migrations and edit admin.service.ts, ro.json and en.json. The new logic therefore lives in new files, and the migration timestamp must be picked right before creating the folder (ls migrations | tail).
SettingsModule is @Global, so RequestsService can inject SettingsService without changing any module imports.

decisions.question: When a client types a phone, email or link in a description or free-text answer, block publishing or hide it from firms?
decisions.chosen_default: New system_settings key pre_claim_contact_text_policy, values MASK|BLOCK, default MASK (migration insert + seed + SETTING_DEFAULTS + admin validator + audit allowlist). MASK: publish succeeds, matches are replaced by ⟦contact⟧ in firm-facing DTOs, hits are logged. BLOCK: 400 REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO_IN_TEXT with per-field details, hits logged as BLOCKED. The client sees the inline hint in both modes.
decisions.why_safe: MASK already enforces docs/03 §4.2 in the API without adding client friction or publish failures from false positives. The stored text is untouched, so switching to BLOCK later (from Admin, no deploy) or back loses nothing.

decisions.question: Should free text also be masked for firms that DID claim but have no contact access (EMPLOYEE_MANAGED not assigned, AFTER_GRACE window)?
decisions.chosen_default: Yes: in QuotesService.getClaimContext, mask title/description/answers/items/scene names whenever access.clientVisible === false, and always mask the title in buildLimitedClaimContext.
decisions.why_safe: docs/03 §4.2 (E-company-3 update) already limits contacts to members with clientVisible; this applies the same boundary to free text.

decisions.question: What happens to a manual title containing contact data?
decisions.chosen_default: Ignore it and use the server auto-title (buildRequestTitle); log a TITLE_REPLACED row. The title never blocks publishing, in either policy.
decisions.why_safe: The UI never sends a manual title (docs/03 §4.1: form fields are finalized by the agent), and the title is pushed to firms in notifications, where read-time masking cannot reach.

decisions.question: What does the detection log store, and for how long?
decisions.chosen_default: Only a redacted excerpt (±60 chars of context, contact partially hidden: phone '07•• ••• •56', email 'a•••@gmail.com', URL host only, handle '@a•••'), plus kinds/field/stepId/roomType/action/trigger. No raw contact value, no user id. Rows are removed only through FK ON DELETE CASCADE with the request; there is no automatic purge.
decisions.why_safe: Keeps new PII to a minimum: the raw text already lives in requests, where the existing GDPR and soft-delete handling covers it. Admins can still tell false positives (a dimension list) from real phone numbers.

decisions.question: Should admins be able to mark a detection as a false positive and unmask that text for firms?
decisions.chosen_default: Not implemented: the admin page is a read-only list (done_when only needs the list). If there are false positives, admins can switch the policy or ask for detector tuning.
decisions.why_safe: An unmask/whitelist action would set a new moderation policy on who can release client text. A read-only list decides nothing.

plan.brief: PACKAGE E-admin-platform-45, Sprint 20 "Pre-claim privacy", finding F2-16. Goal: firms without contact access must not get client phone numbers, emails or links from free text. Read before coding: .claude/skills/prisma-migration, nestjs-module and ui-component (SKILL.md); Codex "BE marketplace", "BE requests", "IMPACT schema Prisma", "IMPACT endpoint nou", "IMPACT text UI"; docs/03 §4.2. === STEP 1 - shared detector (packages/shared/src/contact-detection.ts, NEW; export from src/index.ts) === Exports: - CONTACT_MATCH_KINDS = ['PHONE','EMAIL','URL','HANDLE','MESSENGER'] as const - CONTACT_DETECTION_FIELDS = ['TITLE','DESCRIPTION','ANSWER'] - CONTACT_DETECTION_ACTIONS = ['MASKED','BLOCKED','TITLE_REPLACED','FLAGGED'] - CONTACT_DETECTION_TRIGGERS = ['PUBLISH','EDIT'] - PRE_CLAIM_CONTACT_TEXT_POLICIES = ['MASK','BLOCK'] - SETTING_PRE_CLAIM_CONTACT_TEXT_POLICY = 'pre_claim_contact_text_policy' - CONTACT_MASK_TOKEN = '⟦contact⟧' (renders as ⟦contact⟧) - interface ContactMatch { kind; start; end; text } - detectContactInfo(text: string): ContactMatch[] (sorted, non-overlapping; scan at most the first 20k chars) - isHideable(m) → m.kind !== 'MESSENGER' - maskContactInfo(text: string): string (replaces hideable matches with the token; idempotent) - redactContactExcerpt(text, match, radius = 60): string (context around the match; every hideable match inside the window is redacted: phone keeps the first 2 and last 2 digits, other digits become •, separators kept; email keeps the first local char + '•••@' + domain; URL keeps the host + '/…'; handle keeps '@' + the first char + '•••'; max 240 chars) The existing RO_PHONE_REGEX/INTL_PHONE_REGEX are anchored (^$), so they cannot be reused here. Regexes (all flags g, u where needed; ES2022 target, lookbehind OK): - PHONE candidate: /(?"']+/gi - URL, bare domain: /\b(?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)+(?:ro|com|net|org|eu|info|biz|io|md|co|me|app|shop|store|online|site)\b(?:\/[^\s<>"']*)?/gi (covers wa.me and t.me) - HANDLE: /(? URL > PHONE > HANDLE > MESSENGER, then longer match wins. Tests (contact-detection.test.ts, vitest) are the contract. MUST MATCH: - '0722 123 456', '0722123456', '0722-123-456', '0722.123.456', '+40 722 123 456', '+40722123456', '0040722123456', '021 312 34 56' - '+44 20 7946 0958' - 'ana.popescu@gmail.com', 'ana [at] gmail [dot] com', 'ana arond yahoo.com' - 'www.mobila-ana.ro', 'https://wa.me/40722123456' - 'insta @ana.design' (HANDLE and MESSENGER) - 'scrie-mi pe WhatsApp' (MESSENGER only) MUST NOT MATCH: - '240 x 60 cm', '240x60x35', 'L 2,40 m x l 0,60 m', '0.72 0.60 0.35 2.40', '2400 600 350 mm' - 'buget 15000-20000 lei', '01.10.2026-15.10.2026', '02.10.2026 - 15.10.2026', 'termen 12.03.2026' - '3f2a1b4c-1234-4567-8901-426614174000', 'H=2.6m', 'PAL 18mm', 'blat 38 mm, 3 sertare de 60', '#A0B0C0' - the token itself Also test that maskContactInfo is idempotent and that the redaction never contains the full number or email. === STEP 2 - shared free-text helpers (packages/shared/src/questionnaire/free-text.ts, NEW; export in questionnaire/index.ts) === - collectFreeTextAnswers(roomType, flowVersion, answers): { stepId, path, value }[] - walks flow.steps (all steps, not only visible). type 'text' → string answer. type 'pieces' → each piece's name/description (path 'pieces[i].description'). - maskRoomAnswers(roomType, flowVersion, answers): AnswerMap - returns a new object with maskContactInfo applied to those strings only. If !isFlowVersionRegistered, fall back to a deep walk applying maskContactInfo to every string leaf. The detector boundaries leave UUIDs and hex colours untouched; add a test. - free-text.test.ts: one kitchen text step and one PIECES pieces step; upload-step UUIDs and config3d objects stay unchanged. - error-codes.ts: append REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO_IN_TEXT at the END of the list. - admin.schemas.ts: interface AdminContactDetectionDto { id, requestId, requestTitle, requestStatus, requestDeleted: boolean, trigger, field, roomType: string|null, stepId: string|null, kinds: ContactMatchKind[], excerpt, action, createdAt } and AdminContactDetectionPageDto { items, total, page, pageSize }. - Build: pnpm -F shared build. === STEP 3 - Prisma schema + migration === Model RequestContactDetection (@@map("request_contact_detections")): - id String @id @default(uuid()) - requestId String @map("request_id") - trigger String @db.VarChar(16) - field String @db.VarChar(16) - roomType RoomType? @map("room_type") - stepId String? @map("step_id") @db.VarChar(80) - kinds String[] - excerpt String @db.VarChar(240) - action String @db.VarChar(16) - createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz() - request Request @relation(fields:[requestId], references:[id], onDelete: Cascade) - @@index([requestId]) @@index([createdAt]) Also add `contactDetections RequestContactDetection[]` on Request. Values are validated in the app from the shared const arrays: no new Postgres enums, no CHECK constraints. Migration folder: pick the next free timestamp after the latest (currently 20260930233000; run ls apps/backend/prisma/migrations | tail first), e.g. 20261001001000_request_contact_detections. Generate the SQL with: pnpm -F backend exec prisma migrate diff --from-migrations prisma/migrations --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --shadow-database-url --script Expected SQL: CREATE TABLE "request_contact_detections" (... "kinds" TEXT[], "room_type" "RoomType" NULL ...); two indexes; FK request_id → requests(id) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE; Append by hand: INSERT INTO "system_settings" ("key","value","updated_at") VALUES ('pre_claim_contact_text_policy','MASK',now()) ON CONFLICT ("key") DO NOTHING; -- Rollback: redeploy the previous image; then DELETE FROM system_settings WHERE key='pre_claim_contact_text_policy'; DROP TABLE "request_contact_detections"; Apply and regenerate: pnpm -F backend prisma migrate deploy && pnpm -F backend prisma generate seed.ts: add pre_claim_contact_text_policy: 'MASK' next to claim_contact_reveal_policy (with a comment marking it DECIZIE NECESARA PO). === STEP 4 - settings plumbing === - setting-defaults.ts: pre_claim_contact_text_policy: 'MASK' (comment: E-admin-platform-45, DECIZIE NECESARA PO; BLOCK = publishing refused). - admin.service.ts SETTING_VALUE_RULES: [SETTING_PRE_CLAIM_CONTACT_TEXT_POLICY]: (v) => PRE_CLAIM_CONTACT_TEXT_POLICIES.includes(v) - admin-settings-validation.spec.ts: MASK and BLOCK accepted, 'mask' and 'FOO' rejected. - audit-snapshot.ts: add the key to SETTING_KEYS; settingValue accepts 'MASK'|'BLOCK'. === STEP 5 - backend screening (apps/backend/src/modules/requests/contact-screening.ts, NEW, pure, no Nest) === screenRequestText({ manualTitle?: string, description?: string, rooms: ProcessedRoom[] }) returns: - rows: { field, roomType: RoomType|null, stepId: string|null, kinds: ContactMatchKind[], excerpt, hideable: boolean }[] - at most 20 rows; one row per field/answer that has matches; kinds deduped; excerpt = redactContactExcerpt of the first match. - titleHasContact: boolean - blockingDetails: array of { roomIndex, stepId, messageKey: 'validation.contactInText' } for rooms, plus { field: 'description', messageKey: 'validation.contactInText' } for the description, only for hideable matches. contact-screening.spec.ts: rows, caps, mention-only row has hideable=false, dimensions produce no rows. === STEP 6 - RequestsService (requests.service.ts) === a) Constructor: add `private readonly settings: SettingsService` as the LAST param. Update new RequestsService(...) in requests.service.spec.ts (2 places) and requests.write-rooms.integration.spec.ts (add one more {} as never / settings mock). b) New private async screenContacts(requestId, trigger, dto, processed.rooms) returning { rows ready to insert, titleHasContact }: - Policy = settings.getString(SETTING_PRE_CLAIM_CONTACT_TEXT_POLICY, SETTING_DEFAULTS.pre_claim_contact_text_policy); any unknown value → MASK. - If BLOCK and blockingDetails.length > 0: prisma.requestContactDetection.createMany (outside any transaction), action BLOCKED for hideable rows and FLAGGED for mention-only rows; then throw BadRequestException({ code: ERROR_CODES.REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO_IN_TEXT, message: 'Free text contains contact details', details: blockingDetails }). - Otherwise return the rows with action MASKED (hideable) or FLAGGED; the title row gets TITLE_REPLACED. - The title is never blocked: a manual title with contact data is simply replaced. - Logger: counts and action only, never text (COMMON logging). c) publish(): call it right after assertStudioNightstands and BEFORE geo.geocode (a blocked publish costs no external calls). editRequest(): same place, before the addressChanged geocode, so a blocked edit consumes no edit counter. d) resolveTitle(dto, rooms, titleHasContact): if titleHasContact, return buildRequestTitle(rooms, dto.city). e) Inside the existing $transaction, after writeVersion and before outbox.record: if (rows.length) await tx.requestContactDetection.createMany({ data }). That is one extra query, only for offenders; it keeps the REQUEST_WRITE_TX_OPTIONS budget. requestId = request.id; trigger PUBLISH or EDIT. f) Do NOT change the stored description or answers. Jest cases in requests.service.spec.ts: - MASK plus description 'Sunati la 0722 123 456' → publish resolves; tx createMany called with field DESCRIPTION, kinds ['PHONE'], action MASKED; description written unchanged. - BLOCK → rejects with REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO_IN_TEXT, details [{field:'description',...}], prisma.requestContactDetection.createMany called with BLOCKED, $transaction and geo.geocode NOT called. - description '240 x 60 cm' → no createMany. - manual title 'Bucatarie 0722123456' → written title = auto title, row TITLE_REPLACED. - edit in BLOCK mode → no counter increment. === STEP 7 - read-time masking === New apps/backend/src/common/privacy/contact-masking.ts: - maskFreeText(s: string | null | undefined): string → maskContactInfo(s ?? '') - maskRoomForFirm(room) → { ...room, answers: room.answers ? maskRoomAnswers(room.roomType, room.flowVersion, room.answers) : null, items: items.map(it => ({ ...it, name: maskFreeText(it.name), description: it.description == null ? it.description : maskFreeText(it.description) })) } - maskSceneName(name) Spec file for these helpers. MarketplaceService: - toItem: title: maskFreeText(r.title), description: maskFreeText(r.description). - detail: rooms mapped through maskRoomForFirm; studioScenes name masked. - Always masked in the marketplace, even when alreadyClaimedByMyCompany (the claimed firm reads raw text via by-claim). - marketplace.service.spec.ts: list masks the phone but keeps '240 x 60 cm'; detail masks a text answer, an item description and a scene name; an upload-answer UUID is unchanged. QuotesService.getClaimContext (FULL branch): - const hideText = !access.clientVisible; when true, apply maskFreeText to requestTitle and detail.description, maskRoomForFirm to rooms, maskSceneName to scenes. - buildLimitedClaimContext: mask requestTitle. - quotes.claim-context.spec.ts: EMPLOYEE_MANAGED not assigned → masked; OWNER → raw. === STEP 8 - admin endpoint === - New admin-contact-detections.controller.ts: @Controller('admin/contact-detections') @Roles(UserRole.ADMIN), one @Get() with a query DTO (dto/admin-contact-detections.dto.ts: page and pageSize as @IsOptional @Type(()=>Number) @IsInt @Min(1), pageSize @Max(100); requestId @IsOptional @IsUUID('4')). GET only, so no @Audit and no writes. - New admin-contact-detections.service.ts: findMany orderBy createdAt desc, skip/take, include request { title, status, deletedAt }, plus count → AdminContactDetectionPageDto (admins see the raw request title). - Register both in admin.module.ts. - Spec: pagination clamp and mapping. - Docs: docs/ERROR_CODES.md gets the new code (400, details shape); docs/04 gets an 'Actualizare 2026-10-01 (E-admin-platform-45)' paragraph (table + key); docs/03 §4.2 gets an implementation note with the DECIZIE NECESARA PO on the policy key. === STEP 9 - frontend (after pnpm -F shared build) === a) components/ui/contact-safe-text.tsx: ContactSafeText({ text }) splits on CONTACT_MASK_TOKEN and renders each token as {t('hidden')}; namespace ContactMask. Use it in: - marketplace/page.tsx (title and description, line ~67) - marketplace/[id]/page.tsx (title and description, line ~45) - marketplace/claims/[claimSlotId]/page.tsx (description line ~465 and title) - room-spec-card.tsx (it.name ~197, it.description ~203, notes e.value ~223) - the Studio scene tab name, if simple. b) components/configurator/contact-in-text-hint.tsx: ContactInTextHint({ value }) - useMemo(detectContactInfo); when any match, render an amber note with t('contactInText.hint') (Configurator). Render it under the description Textarea in details-step.tsx and under the text-step Input/Textarea in step-renderer.tsx (line ~451). c) review-step.tsx: - serverRoomIssues already reads {roomIndex, stepId, messageKey} for any code. - Add: when apiErr === 'REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO_IN_TEXT' and details contain field 'description', show t('contactInText.descriptionIssue') plus the existing edit-details button (onEditDetails). Include it in the condition at line ~325. d) Admin: - layout NAV: { href: '/admin/contact-detections', key: 'contactDetections' } - use-admin.ts: useContactDetections(page) → api('/admin/contact-detections?page=..&pageSize=25') - New page app/[locale]/admin/contact-detections/page.tsx (copy the audit page table/pager pattern).
