fixes_made: packages/shared/src/contact-detection.ts: the detector was slow on long inputs. EMAIL_RE, EMAIL_OBFUSCATED_RE and BARE_DOMAIN_RE used unbounded quantifiers, so running time grew with the square of the text length (about 150 ms for a 5,000-character description, 2-3.4 s at the 20k scan cap). maskContactInfo runs on every marketplace list and detail item, so one client could slow down every firm's marketplace page. I capped the lengths: local part {1,64}, labels {1,63}, at most 8 domain labels, TLD {2,24}, and \s{0,3} in the obfuscated form. The same inputs now take 1-15 ms at 20k characters, and all 338 previous shared tests still pass.
packages/shared/src/contact-detection.test.ts: added a performance regression test (20k characters of letters, dots, or '@' followed by dots must each finish under 500 ms).
remaining_issues: Not verified live over HTTP or in the browser. Every done-when step that needs a demo login (curl login, HTTP edit/marketplace/admin checks, BLOCK→FOO→MASK via the API, the browser chip/admin page/configurator hint) needs a password entered into the login endpoint. Only the user in chat can authorize that; a workflow script cannot. Those steps were checked instead through DB state from the implementer's run, function-level runs of the built shared package, unit/spec tests and unauthenticated 401/200 checks. The user can run the curl/browser steps, or authorize them in chat.

The backend dev server (nest --watch) may not reload when only packages/shared/dist changes, so it may still run the old detector code until it restarts. Behaviour is the same for normal inputs; only speed on long adversarial text differs.

In BLOCK mode every refused attempt writes BLOCKED rows outside a transaction (at most 20 per attempt), and there is no per-request dedupe. A client retrying in a loop can grow the table. The throttler likely limits this, but it was not checked.

Scanning stops after MAX_SCAN_CHARS=20000. Today's limits (description 5000, answers bounded by schemas) keep inputs under that, but a longer field in the future would leave contacts after 20k unmasked.

The implementer's open PO decisions still stand: the MASK vs BLOCK policy (default MASK) and a false-positive/unmask action for admins. Also out of scope: deep masking of house/room labels inside the Studio scene data, and re-masking legacy manual titles in the firm's 'my claims' list.

plan.summary:
Implementation plan for E-client-9 (Sprint 20, pre-claim privacy). SEC1-12 (contacts typed into free text) was already delivered by E-admin-platform-45 on 2026-10-01: detector, MASK/BLOCK setting, ContactInTextHint and admin log. So SEC1-12 only needs re-verification. Remaining work:
(1) C7-2: marketplace visibility, distance and the claim coverage check are computed from the request point snapped to a fixed grid of about 2 km (cell centre, floor-based, identical in SQL and TS). Distance is returned as whole km plus a band; a new setting `marketplace_distance_display` (KM by default, BAND optional) decides which one firms see. Location writes get a 2 km minimum radius (shared constant), a location cap and a rolling 24h change limit (both system_settings), and are audited through @Audit + AuditInterceptor.
(2) C7-3: add sharp 0.35.4 as a backend dependency. The uploads scan worker re-encodes jpeg/png/webp (EXIF and GPS stripped, orientation applied) into a neutral key with no filename. Sealed keys also stop carrying the filename. Firm-facing attachment lists (marketplace detail, by-claim) get the neutral name `attachment-N.ext` and a matching Content-Disposition. A startup job re-processes legacy SAFE REQUEST files. Upload and review copy warn that files are visible to firms before a claim.
(3) C7-11: rewrite the privacy sections `data` and `sharing` in RO and EN: add phone, EXIF stripping, what firms see before a claim, and that the account email is always shared. Nominatim is already named.
(4) C7-16: new GET /requests/:id/visibility (client owner) and a 'Cine vede cererea' card on /requests/[id].
The only DB change is a data-only migration that inserts 3 system_settings rows. No schema change.
modules: backend marketplace (SQL geometry, DTO distance, neutral attachment names)
backend companies (location min radius, cap, change limit, audit)
backend uploads + infra/storage (EXIF strip in scan worker, neutral keys, presigned Content-Disposition, legacy backfill job)
backend quotes (by-claim neutral attachment names; export contact-access settings reader)
backend admin + common/settings (new setting keys + validation)
frontend company dashboard (location form min radius + api errors)
frontend messages ro.json/en.json (Legal.privacy data+sharing, new keys)
tables: requests (read only: lat/lng snapped at query time, never rewritten)
company_locations (read; create/update/delete now capped, radius floor, change-limited)
claim_slots (read: occupying slots for visibility endpoint)
companies (read: name for visibility card)
attachments (update storage_key + size_bytes after sanitize; status transitions unchanged)
audit_logs (insert COMPANY_LOCATION_* rows via interceptor; read count for 24h change limit)
system_settings (3 new rows: marketplace_distance_display, company_locations_max, company_location_changes_per_day)
files: apps/backend/package.json (+ pnpm-lock.yaml via pnpm add sharp@0.35.4)

Codex: 10 Module BE/BE marketplace.md, BE uploads.md, BE companies.md, BE requests.md, BE claims.md, INFRA storage.md, 40 Concepte/CONCEPT uploads.md, 20 Frontend/FE marketplace firma.md, FE client cereri si oferte.md, FE configurator.md
assumptions: SEC1-12 is already delivered by E-admin-platform-45 (CHANGELOG 2026-10-01, docs/03 4.2 note; files contact-detection.ts, contact-masking.ts, contact-in-text-hint.tsx exist). This package only re-verifies it and does not rebuild it.

The privacy text already names Nominatim (E-admin-platform-2). C7-11 is therefore reduced to: add phone, say who sees what before and after a claim, mention that the account email is always shared, and describe EXIF stripping.

The approved plan step 'compute pre-claim distance and visibility from a snapped ~2 km point' authorizes measuring D-v6-10 coverage against the approximate client point. The marketplace SQL and the claim transaction use the same snapped point, so they cannot diverge.

Grid cell centre with floor(): LAT step 0.018 deg (~2.0 km), LNG step 0.026 deg (~1.9-2.1 km across Romania). A request can move at most about 1.45 km. Floor + 0.5 gives identical IEEE results in JS and Postgres (round() tie rules differ, so it is not used).
Only request coordinates are snapped. Firm locations stay exact because they are the firm's own data.

sharp 0.35.4 is already in the pnpm store and the lockfile, including the @img/sharp-linux-x64 binaries. The Docker image is node:22-bookworm-slim (glibc), so the prebuilt binaries work without Dockerfile changes.
Image processing in the BullMQ worker does not violate invariant 3.4: no file bytes pass through an HTTP endpoint, and the worker reads from storage the way a real antivirus would.
LEGAL_PRIVACY_VERSION 2026-09-29 is not live on prod yet (CHANGELOG notes it as undelivered; prod is still on release/2026-09-17), so the rewrite does not bump it.
No new Postgres enums or columns. The new settings are TEXT rows in system_settings, validated in the app.

Firm-facing neutral names apply only to REQUEST attachments in the marketplace detail and in GET /quotes/by-claim. The client owner and chat keep original names. EXIF stripping applies to every new image upload of any entity type.

decisions.question: Before a claim, should phone numbers and emails typed into descriptions be hidden from firms?
decisions.chosen_default: Already implemented and documented in docs/03 4.2 (E-admin-platform-45): MASK by default through system_settings.pre_claim_contact_text_policy, with BLOCK available. Nothing to change; only re-verify.
decisions.why_safe: The rule is already written in docs/03 4.2 and shipped; the MASK/BLOCK choice is tracked as that package's own DECIZIE NECESARA and is not reopened here.

decisions.question: Before a claim, should distance be shown only as bands (<5, 5-15, 15-30, 30+ km) instead of whole km?
decisions.chosen_default: New setting marketplace_distance_display = 'KM' (default): whole km computed from the snapped point (min 1). 'BAND' sets distanceKm=null and firms see only distanceBand. The DTO always includes distanceBand. There are no marketplace filters today, so filtering is unaffected.
decisions.why_safe: Whole km on a point snapped to about 2 km already removes the 100 m precision needed for trilateration. Bands can be switched on from Admin without a deploy, and nothing is stored or lost either way.

decisions.question: What minimum coverage radius should a firm location have (the finding suggests 5 km; docs/07 D-v6-10 only sets the default of 50)?
decisions.chosen_default: Shared constant MIN_COVERAGE_RADIUS_KM = 2 (equal to the privacy grid cell; a smaller radius means nothing once points are snapped), enforced in the DTO and the zod schema on create/update only. Existing rows are not rewritten (local data is all 50/100 km).
decisions.why_safe: This is a technical floor tied to the grid, not a commercial rule. It does not affect current firms. PO can raise it to 5.

decisions.question: How many locations can a firm have, and how often can it change them (the finding suggests a cap per plan plus a cooldown)?
decisions.chosen_default: Global settings company_locations_max = 10 and company_location_changes_per_day = 20 (rolling 24h, counted from audit_logs rows COMPANY_LOCATION_* for the company). New errors: 409 COMPANY_LOCATION_LIMIT_REACHED and 429 COMPANY_LOCATION_CHANGE_LIMIT. No per-plan differentiation.
decisions.why_safe: Every firm has exactly 1 location today, so neither limit is close. Both are anti-abuse limits that can be changed from Admin, and no plan or price is touched.

decisions.question: Does the privacy policy rewrite require bumping LEGAL_PRIVACY_VERSION, which forces every user to re-accept?
decisions.chosen_default: Keep 2026-09-29. That version has not been deployed yet, so no user has accepted a different text under it.
decisions.why_safe: Avoids a re-acceptance dialog for text nobody accepted yet. If 2026-09-29 reaches prod before this package, the version must be bumped. The legal text still needs PO and lawyer review (IMPACT text UI, point 9).

decisions.question: What counts as a firm that 'holds the contacts' on the 'Cine vede cererea' card?
decisions.chosen_default: docs/03 4.2: occupying slot (ACTIVE, OFFER_SENT, COMPLETED) on a non-deleted request. With claim_contact_reveal_policy=AFTER_GRACE the card shows 'from {time}' (claim createdAt + VOLUNTARY_WITHDRAWAL_GRACE_MS). This reuses resolveClaimContextAccess with firm-level role OWNER.
decisions.why_safe: Reuses the exact access function the by-claim endpoint uses, so the card cannot contradict what firms actually receive.

decisions.question: What neutral filename should firms see, and should PDF/ZIP metadata also be stripped?
decisions.chosen_default: Name 'attachment-{n}.{ext}' (n = 1-based position by createdAt), also used in the presigned GET's Content-Disposition. Images are re-encoded; PDF/ZIP are only moved to a neutral key. The upload notice tells clients to keep names and addresses out of plans.
decisions.why_safe: Purely technical. No business rule is involved, the owner keeps the original name, and PDF metadata stripping stays a documented follow-up.

3. PRE-CLAIM GEOMETRY (C7-2)
- New apps/backend/src/common/privacy/location-privacy.ts:
  - `PRIVACY_GRID_LAT_DEG = 0.018`, `PRIVACY_GRID_LNG_DEG = 0.026`
  - `snapToPrivacyGrid(lat, lng) => ({ lat: (Math.floor(lat / LAT) + 0.5) * LAT, lng: (Math.floor(lng / LNG) + 0.5) * LNG })`
  - `wholeKm(d) = Math.max(1, Math.round(d))`
  - Comment: identical formula in SQL (floor, not round, for JS/PG parity).
  - Spec: determinism; |snapped - original| <= ~1.5 km for Bucuresti/Cluj points; two points in the same cell give the same output; wholeKm(0.2) = 1.
- marketplace.service.ts queryRows: add before the distance lateral
  `CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT (floor(r.lat / ${PRIVACY_GRID_LAT_DEG}::float8) + 0.5) * ${PRIVACY_GRID_LAT_DEG}::float8 AS lat, (floor(r.lng / ${PRIVACY_GRID_LNG_DEG}::float8) + 0.5) * ${PRIVACY_GRID_LNG_DEG}::float8 AS lng) rp`
  and replace r.lat/r.lng with rp.lat/rp.lng inside the Haversine. Keep the `r.lat IS NOT NULL` filters and `per_loc.dist <= per_loc.radius`.

5. UPLOADS: EXIF + NEUTRAL NAMES (C7-3)
- `pnpm -F backend add sharp@0.35.4 --prefer-offline` (the root override already pins ^0.35.4). Check with `pnpm -F backend exec node -e "require('sharp')"`.
- storage.service.ts:
  - `getObjectBytes(key, maxBytes)`: GetObjectCommand, `Body.transformToByteArray()`, throw if longer than maxBytes.
  - `putObject(key, body: Buffer, contentType)`.
  - `getPresignedDownloadUrl(key, opts?: { downloadName?: string })`: when set, `ResponseContentDisposition: inline; filename="<ascii-safe>"`.
- New uploads/image-sanitizer.ts:
  - `SANITIZABLE_IMAGE_MIME = ['image/jpeg','image/png','image/webp']`;
  - `sanitizeImage(buf, mime)` builds `sharp(buf, { failOn: 'error', limitInputPixels: 40_000_000, animated: mime === 'image/webp' }).rotate()` and then `.jpeg({ quality: 88 })`, `.png()` or `.webp({ quality: 88 })`. Never call withMetadata/keepExif, so sharp strips metadata by default;
  - set `sharp.cache(false); sharp.concurrency(1)` at module level;
  - returns Buffer.
- uploads.service.ts:
  - confirm(): sealedKey becomes ``${entityType.toLowerCase()}/${entityId}/${attachment.id}/sealed-${randomUUID()}${extForMime(mime)}``, with no filename. Leave the presign key as is: it is deleted after sealing and only the uploader sees it.
  - scan(): keep the current checks. If not blocked and the mime is sanitizable:
    - `bytes = await storage.getObjectBytes(key, MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES)`;
    - try sanitizeImage; on a decode error, updateMany to BLOCKED (log only the id) and return;
    - if the output is larger than MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES, BLOCKED;
    - cleanKey = `.../${id}/clean-${uuid}.${ext}`; putObject;
    - `updateMany({ where: { id, status: 'PENDING_SCAN', storageKey: oldKey }, data: { status: 'SAFE', storageKey: cleanKey, sizeBytes: out.length } })`;
    - count 0 → deleteObject(cleanKey); else deleteObject(oldKey) best effort.
    PDF/ZIP keep the current path unchanged. Storage errors are thrown so BullMQ retries.
  - listForEntity(entityType, entityId, tx?, opts?: { neutralNames?: boolean }) and toDto(row, neutralName?): filename = `attachment-${i+1}.${ext}` and downloadUrl signed with downloadName.
  - New `sanitizeLegacyRequestAttachments(batch = 50)`: selects REQUEST SAFE rows whose storageKey does not match `/\/(clean|sealed)-[0-9a-f-]{36}(\.[a-z0-9]+)?$/`. Images go through the same sanitize-to-clean-key path, conditional on `status: 'SAFE'` plus the old key. PDF/ZIP, or images that fail to decode, are copied with sealObject into a neutral sealed key. Returns whether more rows remain.
- uploads.processor.ts:
  - onModuleInit adds job `sanitize.legacy` with jobId `upload-legacy-sanitize`;

plan.summary:
E-admin-platform-54 is partly done already. E-company-2 (2026-09-29) already set a global Prisma transactionOptions of maxWait 5 s / timeout 20 s (infra/prisma/tx-options.ts WRITE_TX_OPTIONS, applied in the PrismaService constructor). That means payments.confirm, cancel and subscriptions.adminGrant already run on 20 s, which covers the "do_first" item. The filter also already maps P2028 and P2024 to 503 DATABASE_BUSY with Retry-After: 2 and a warn log.

Four things are still missing:
(a) There is no single runTx(profile) helper. The backend has 63 bare prisma.$transaction call sites (4 of them batch form), no lint ban on them, and 2 Serializable transactions without in-process retry: offer-expiry-settlement.processor and fulfillment completeDelivered.
(b) P1001 and P1017 are not mapped, and DB-busy errors reach Sentry at error level.
(c) In payments.confirm, the invoice advisory lock covers the benefit grant and the members read.
(d) The frontend has no automatic retry and no 'Serverul e ocupat, reîncercăm' feedback. DATABASE_BUSY copy exists in only 3 of 13 apiErrors namespaces.

No migration is needed. The package reuses the existing ERROR_CODES.DATABASE_BUSY instead of adding SERVICE_BUSY.
modules: backend infra/prisma (new tx.ts helper, tx-options profiles)
backend billing (payments.service confirm/cancel + all tx sites, subscriptions.service adminGrant, subscription-expiry.processor, billing-readiness batch)

backend claims (claims.service, claims.helpers re-export, claims.constants re-export, withdrawals, clarifications, claim-assign/sla-breach/offer-expiry-settlement/reconciliation/withdrawal-reminder processors)
backend companies, auth/token.service, chat, inspiration/boards, uploads (mechanical tx conversion)
backend lint config (.eslintrc.cjs ban on bare $transaction)
frontend hooks/use-idempotent-api (retry once on DATABASE_BUSY + toast)
frontend messages ro.json/en.json (Common.serverBusyRetrying + DATABASE_BUSY in 10 more apiErrors namespaces)
tables: none altered (no schema change)
runtime-touched, semantics unchanged: mock_billing_orders, company_credit_wallets, credit_transactions, subscriptions, company_members (read), domain_event_outbox, idempotency_keys
assumptions: E-company-2 already shipped these: global transactionOptions {maxWait 5 s, timeout 20 s} in PrismaService, P2028/P2024 mapped to 503 DATABASE_BUSY with Retry-After: 2 and a warn log, and DATABASE_BUSY copy in Requests/Marketplace/Quotes. This package builds on that and does not redo it.
ERROR_CODES.DATABASE_BUSY is the 'server busy' code the plan calls SERVICE_BUSY. Adding a second code with the same meaning would split FE mapping and logs, so no new shared code is added.

Prisma 5.19 merges per-call transaction options per key with the client defaults, so a profile that sets timeout 10 s keeps 10 s. Invariant 3.1 (docs/02 line 9: claim is Serializable with a 10 s timeout) stays enforced by the 'claim' profile.
P1001 arrives as PrismaClientInitializationError (field errorCode, not code). P1017 arrives as PrismaClientKnownRequestError code P1017. Both are handled.

All 10 @Idempotent endpoints are {transactional: true}. After a raw Prisma error the interceptor rethrows and the receipt stays at responseStatus 0, so a same-key retry reuses the receipt. lockIdempotentOperation replays when a previous attempt committed, so one automatic FE retry cannot double-apply an effect.

payments.confirm must stay READ COMMITTED. Invoice numbering takes MAX()+1 under pg_advisory_xact_lock, and under Serializable/RepeatableRead the snapshot is taken before the lock wait. A waiting confirm would then read a stale MAX and hit a duplicate number or a 40001 error. So confirm uses the 'write' profile, not 'critical'.
Local test DB marketplace_test exists (Codex INFRA prisma, E-company-2 gotcha). If it is missing, create it with createdb in the postgres container and run migrate deploy against it.
On Windows the backend dev server may need REDIS_HOST=127.0.0.1 (Codex gotcha). Do not edit apps/backend/.env.

decisions.question: New ERROR_CODES.SERVICE_BUSY (as the plan text says) or reuse the existing DATABASE_BUSY?
decisions.chosen_default: Reuse DATABASE_BUSY (already in packages/shared/src/error-codes.ts, the filter, specs and 3 i18n namespaces). Extend it to P1001/P1017 and add its copy to the other namespaces.
decisions.why_safe: Same meaning, no API contract change, no duplicate code for the FE to map. The acceptance intent (503 + Retry-After + warn + FE retry) is met exactly.

decisions.question: Transaction timeouts env-tunable per region (proposed_fix) or constants?
decisions.chosen_default: Constants in infra/prisma/tx-options.ts (TX_PROFILES). No new env vars in this package.
decisions.why_safe: New env vars would need to be set on both blue/green slots (IMPACT env si deploy). The global 20 s default already absorbs the cross-region latency. The EU migration plan is only PROPUS. Constants are trivially changeable later.

decisions.question: Claim transaction timeout under the new profiles
decisions.chosen_default: 'claim' profile = Serializable, timeout 10_000 (CLAIM_TX_TIMEOUT_MS), maxWait 5_000, serialization retry. Used by every site that uses CLAIM_TX_TIMEOUT_MS today. A tx.spec test pins the 10 s value.
decisions.why_safe: docs/02-technical-invariants.md line 9 (invariant 3.1) mandates Serializable with a 10 s timeout. Longer timeouts would hold claim locks longer (plan 'risks').

decisions.question: Should payments.confirm move to Serializable ('critical')?
decisions.chosen_default: No. confirm and cancel use the 'write' profile (READ COMMITTED, 20 s). The row FOR UPDATE, the advisory lock and the conditional updateMany keep their current race-safety.
decisions.why_safe: Snapshot isolation plus MAX()+1 behind an advisory lock would read a stale MAX. Keeping today's isolation changes nothing about the fiscal numbering (docs/03 4.17).

decisions.question: How far to shorten the invoice advisory-lock window in confirm without breaking 4.17 sequential numbering
decisions.chosen_default: Read company members before the transaction. Inside it: row lock, then status updateMany (count check), then benefit grant (credits/subscription), then advisory lock, then aggregate, then invoice update, then outbox. confirmedAt (and paidAt when extra.paidAt is absent) is stamped AFTER the advisory lock in the invoice update, so invoice numbers stay monotonic with issue timestamps.
decisions.why_safe: docs/03 4.17 requires continuous sequential numbering per series. Stamping the date under the lock keeps number order equal to date order, as today, and all writes stay in one transaction.

decisions.question: Should DB-busy errors still go to the error tracker?
decisions.chosen_default: Yes, but at Sentry level 'warning' (new optional level parameter on captureServerException). The log stays logger.warn in the existing format.
decisions.why_safe: Meets done_when 'timeouts listed as warnings, separate from real bugs' without losing the operational signal. Only tracker severity changes, no business rule.

decisions.question: Which calls retry automatically on DATABASE_BUSY?
decisions.chosen_default: Only useIdempotentApi (the 10 @Idempotent transactional POSTs): exactly one retry after 2 s (matching Retry-After: 2) with the same Idempotency-Key, and a toast 'Serverul e ocupat, reîncercăm…'. Plain api() calls (e.g. publish, admin confirm) are not auto-retried; they show the DATABASE_BUSY copy.
decisions.why_safe: Only idempotent-receipt endpoints are safe against an unknown-outcome failure (P1017 during commit). Matches plan step 5 and acceptance 3.

decisions.question: Should the idempotency lock be bundled into runTx profiles (proposed_fix)?
decisions.chosen_default: No. lockIdempotentOperation stays explicit at each call site.
decisions.why_safe: Idempotent requests run several transactions (e.g. createPendingOrder saves a checkpoint, then attachCheckout saves the result). Taking the receipt lock automatically in every transaction would throw IdempotentReplay in later transactions of the same request once a result is saved.

  export function runTx<T>(prisma: TxHost, profile: TxProfile, fn: (tx: Prisma.TransactionClient) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {

    const once = () => prisma.$transaction(fn, options);

I've planned E-admin-platform-14 (Sprint 21) against the current tree. The code has moved on since the audit, so several findings are already partly fixed:
- A pure `computeSizing()` that already returns `baseScore` exists, along with `sizing.service.spec.ts` (E-admin-platform-25).

- Retries are now 3 with jitter (the audit said 1).

What is still true:
- No real-DB test takes a claim to a terminal state or checks the ledger for each firm.

decisions.question: Should the budget estimate (POST /requests/estimate minRon) use the base score instead of the total score?
decisions.chosen_default: Yes. SizingResult gains baseScore, and estimate() uses minRon = baseScore * BUDGET_RON_PER_POINT and returns score = baseScore.
decisions.why_safe: PO r5 V1 (docs/archive/15-feedback-po-r5-sprints.md) defines the minimum budget as the base score × 1,000 RON, with cost = minRon/1000. It only equals the total score today because BUDGET:UNDISCLOSED weighs 0, and that weight is now editable in /admin/sizing. Output is identical on the current data.

decisions.question: Drop project_size_thresholds.credit_cost now, as the package step says?
decisions.chosen_default: Expand only in this sprint: ALTER COLUMN credit_cost DROP NOT NULL, Prisma field becomes Int? (with a legacy comment), and seed.ts stops writing it. The DROP COLUMN goes in a separate later release, once neither blue/green slot runs an image whose Prisma client selects the column as a non-null Int.
decisions.why_safe: IMPACT schema Prisma rule 2 (blue/green: both slots read the same DB) forbids a DROP in the same release. The old image's projectSizeThreshold.findMany selects the column and would fail, which would break publish and estimate on the standby/rollback slot. PO r5 decision #3 also said 'no destructive migration'.

decisions.question: PO question: may the later contract release run `ALTER TABLE project_size_thresholds DROP COLUMN credit_cost`, overriding r5 decision #3 ('the column stays, no destructive migration')?
decisions.chosen_default: Not done in this sprint; only the nullable expand step ships.
decisions.why_safe: Nothing reads the column. Leaving it nullable costs nothing and keeps rollback possible.

decisions.question: docs/03 §4.8 (lines 60/62/90) and docs/07 D-v6-5 still say claim cost = 1/2/4 credits per size from project_size_thresholds, while code follows PO r5 (1 credit = 1,000 RON of minimum budget). Should they be amended?
decisions.chosen_default: Do not edit docs/07 (decisions are FINAL) or the pricing text in docs/03. Update only docs/04 line 50 (column marked legacy/nullable, with a pointer to creditCostFromBaseScore), and flag the conflict to the PO in CHANGELOG under 'DECIZIE NECESARA'.
decisions.why_safe: No business text changes without the PO. The code keeps its current behaviour, and the new tests pin that behaviour so any later pricing change is deliberate.

decisions.question: Should the table-driven claim-cost tests include the planned 3..25 clamp mentioned in the finding?
decisions.chosen_default: No. The tests pin the current formula (0→1, negative→1, 0.4→1, 1→1, 12→12, 12.5→13, 33→33). The clamp belongs to the future pricing sprint and is not in docs/03 or docs/07.
decisions.why_safe: The tests only describe current behaviour. No price or policy is invented.

decisions.question: What coverage floor is 'agreed' for billing, claims and requests?
decisions.chosen_default: A ratchet floor: after the new tests land, run `pnpm -F backend test:cov`, take the lines/branches/functions per folder, round down, subtract 2 and use the result. It must never be below the pre-sprint baseline (billing L60/B55/F50, claims L78/B70/F68, requests L57/B43/F44). Report the final numbers in CHANGELOG.
decisions.why_safe: This is an engineering gate, not a business rule. The floor starts at the measured value so CI does not break, and it stops regressions.

decisions.question: Which database hosts may integration tests use?
decisions.chosen_default: A fixed allow-list: localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 / [::1], and the compose service name 'postgres'. The protocol must be postgres: or postgresql:. There is no environment-variable override. The refusal message names only the hostname, never the credentials.
decisions.why_safe: It matches the scripts/house-acceptance.cjs guard and the CI setup (127.0.0.1). Any hosted DB (*.rlwy.net, *.railway.internal, etc.) is refused.

decisions.question: Per-spec isolation: a dedicated schema or transaction per spec (finding R2-TESTS-15), or id-scoped cleanup?
decisions.chosen_default: Id-scoped cleanup (the existing pattern) with a unique 'E14 ' prefix. No schema-per-spec.
decisions.why_safe: The concurrency tests need real committed transactions and separate connections, so wrapping each spec in a transaction would defeat them. The existing specs already use this pattern.

decisions.question: How should penalties be asserted when the CI DB has no penalty_rules?
decisions.chosen_default: Read the rule's points first (SLA_MISS, VOLUNTARY_WITHDRAWAL). Expect exactly one penalty_event when points > 0 and none otherwise. The credit outcome is always asserted strictly.
decisions.why_safe: No global config rows are created in the shared dev DB.

decisions.question: Should @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any be enabled for all specs?
decisions.chosen_default: Only through an .eslintrc override for src/test/**, claims.test-fixtures.ts and the three new *.integration.spec.ts files. The existing specs keep their current disable comments.
decisions.why_safe: No existing lint breaks. New harness code is typed, so a constructor-order change becomes a compile error.

E-admin-platform-14: Test credit money flows against a real database (Sprint 21, P2, ~5 days)

Repo: F:\Cozy Fable (Git Bash: /f/Cozy\ Fable). Work only in the files listed here. Never commit, push, stash, checkout or reset. Never edit apps/backend/.env or docs/07. Code comments are in Romanian without diacritics.

This package has no UI, i18n, endpoint or error-code changes.

READ FIRST
- The testing section of .claude/skills/nestjs-module/SKILL.md, and .claude/skills/prisma-migration/SKILL.md.
- Codex: "50 Impact/IMPACT credite.md" (points 2, 3, 7, 8, 9), "IMPACT accept si claim.md" (lock 3.1 and the order inside the transaction), "IMPACT schema Prisma.md" (points 1-4, 7, 13), "10 Module BE/BE sizing.md".
- The model spec to copy: apps/backend/src/modules/quotes/quotes.concurrency.integration.spec.ts. It shows real PrismaService with an explicit url, SettingsService, CreditsService, OutboxService(prisma, {publish}), stub queues {add, remove}, calendar stub {addWorkingDays}, a $use latency/in-tx counter, the makeCompany/makeSlot/cleanup helpers, and `settlementsOf`.

Money rules the tests must encode (IMPACT credite point 3, D-L0-3, pay-to-play):
- voluntary withdraw < 30 min → REFUND
- voluntary withdraw ≥ 30 min → CONSUME, plus the VOLUNTARY_WITHDRAWAL penalty
- unassigned for 1 h (claim-assign) → CANCELLED_UNASSIGNED + REFUND
- SLA missed (deadline + SLA_GRACE_MS passed) → SLA_EXPIRED + CONSUME, plus the SLA_MISS penalty
- accept: losing slots that sent an offer → CANCELLED_REQUEST_ACCEPTED + CONSUME (their quote becomes SUPERSEDED); losing ACTIVE slots without an offer → REFUND
- winner → CONSUME with reason 'COMPLETED' on confirmDelivery, or on autoCompleteDelivered 14 days after delivered_at
- client deletes the request → every ACTIVE/OFFER_SENT slot → CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT + REFUND

Every RESERVE gets exactly one REFUND or CONSUME once the slot is closed. Credits move only through CreditsService. Never write to company_credit_wallets directly, not even in fixtures: create the wallet with balance 0, then credits.grant.

- (a) Claim: slot ACTIVE, claimCostCreditsSnapshot 2, one RESERVE; wallet balance 18, reserved 2; request status CLAIMED_PARTIAL; one outbox row 'claim.created:<slot>'.
- (b1) Withdraw < 30 min: withdrawals.request(ctx, owner, slot, { reasonType:'VOLUNTARY_NO_REASON' }) → one REFUND; wallet back to 20/0; request back to IN_MARKETPLACE.
- (b2) Withdraw ≥ 30 min: backdate claim_slots.created_at by 31 min, pass expectedOutcome 'CONSUME_AND_PENALTY' → one CONSUME, wallet 18/0. Penalty: if the VOLUNTARY_WITHDRAWAL rule has points > 0, exactly one penalty_event for the slot, otherwise 0.
- (b3) A second withdraw on the same slot → 409 CLAIM_NOT_WITHDRAWABLE; the ledger does not change.
- (c) Auto-cancel when unassigned: claim with no assignee; backdate assign_deadline_at to now−1 min; `claimAssign.process({ name:'assign-deadline', data:{claimSlotId} } as Job)` → CANCELLED_UNASSIGNED + one REFUND with reason 'CLAIM_AUTO_CANCEL_UNASSIGNED'. Calling it again → still exactly one REFUND.
- (d) SLA breach: backdate sla_deadline_at to now − SLA_GRACE_MS − 1 min (import the constant); `slaBreach.process({ name:'breach', data:{claimSlotId} } as Job)` → SLA_EXPIRED + one CONSUME with 'SLA_BREACH'; the SLA_MISS penalty is conditional as in (b2); calling again → no second CONSUME.
- (e) Accept with losers: three firms A, B and C claim. A and B create quotes via quotes.createQuote; C stays ACTIVE with no offer. The client calls acceptQuote(client, quoteA, quoteA.versions[0].id). Expect:
  - request ACCEPTED
  - A: OFFER_SENT with 0 settlements (still reserved)
  - B: CANCELLED_REQUEST_ACCEPTED + one CONSUME; its quote SUPERSEDED
  - C: CANCELLED_REQUEST_ACCEPTED + one REFUND
- (f) Completion by the client: continue (e): fulfillment.markDelivered(ctxA, requestId), then confirmDelivery(client, requestId) → request COMPLETED; A's slot COMPLETED with one CONSUME 'COMPLETED'. A second confirmDelivery → 409 COMPLETION_NOT_ALLOWED with no second CONSUME.
- (f2) Auto-complete: same setup, then backdate delivered_at by 15 days → autoCompleteDelivered(requestId) returns true; one CONSUME; a second call returns false.
- (g) Client deletes the request: A claims and makes an offer (OFFER_SENT), B claims (ACTIVE); requests.deleteForClient(client, requestId) → both CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT with one REFUND each (reason REQUEST_DELETED_BY_CLIENT); A's quote WITHDRAWN; request.deletedAt set.

sprint: Sprint 22 - Settle-once credits and credit rules

plan.summary: Plan for E-admin-platform-15 (Sprint 22). All credit refunds and consumptions move into one ClaimSettlementService.settle() in the billing module. It checks the ledger first, so a slot with no RESERVE row (demo or legacy data), a slot that is already settled, or a wallet that cannot cover the amount still gets its status change but no wallet movement. This fixes the 4 local SLA-breach jobs that failed permanently on the reserved >= 0 CHECK. All 7 caller files (9 call sites) plus the 2 existing settleClaimSlot users move onto settle(). An ESLint rule bans credits.refund/consume everywhere else. A shared CreditReason list is added in packages/shared. There are 2 SQL-only migrations: partial unique indexes on credit_transactions(claim_slot_id) for RESERVE and for REFUND/CONSUME, and VALIDATE of both wallet CHECKs. A daily ledger-vs-wallet check runs on the existing reconciliation queue, with a read-only admin endpoint and a bell alert to admins. Local pre-checks were run: 0 duplicate settlements, 0 duplicate reserves, 0 negative wallets, both CHECKs are still NOT VALID, and reserved matches the ledger for every wallet. Balances differ only for demo firms, which were seeded without GRANT rows.
modules: claims (claim-assign, sla-breach, withdrawals, offer-expiry-settlement, reconciliation, settlement.ts removal)
tables: credit_transactions (2 new partial UNIQUE indexes, SQL-only; reason stays String)
company_credit_wallets (VALIDATE CONSTRAINT balance_nonneg + reserved_nonneg)
claim_slots (no schema change; transitions now all via settle())
claim_withdrawals (refunded flag now follows the real settlement outcome)

Local DB pre-check, run read-only on 2026-09-30: 0 slots with more than one REFUND/CONSUME, 0 with more than one RESERVE, 0 wallets with a negative value. Both *_nonneg constraints are convalidated=false. The production pre-check (do_first) cannot be run from here, so it is written into the migration header and the CHANGELOG as an operator step before applying migrations on prod.
The 4 failing local sla-breach jobs (sla-e28ed141…, sla-1f006ef3…, sla-e2438857…, sla-ef1051f0…) all belong to seed-demo ACTIVE slots with no RESERVE row in the ledger. That is the root of LIVE-11.

Every current caller uses CreditsService only for refund/consume, except claims.service (reserve) and payments/subscriptions (grant). So the CreditsService constructor parameter can be swapped in place for ClaimSettlementService without reordering constructor arguments.
Every module that settles already imports BillingModule, so putting ClaimSettlementService in billing creates no new module cycle.
credit_transactions.reason stays a String column. Historical prod rows keep their values; the shared list only types new writes.
Business outcomes do not change: which path REFUNDs and which CONSUMEs stays exactly as in IMPACT credite §3. No price, duration or business number changes. docs/07 is not touched.

decisions.question: What does settlement do when a slot has no RESERVE row in the ledger (seed-demo or legacy data)? This is the direct cause of LIVE-11.
decisions.chosen_default: Commit the status transition (for example SLA_EXPIRED), apply the penalty and send notifications as usual, but move no credits and write no ledger row. Return credit='SKIPPED_NO_RESERVE' and refunded=false, and log a warning.
decisions.why_safe: docs/02 §3.1 says every claim inserts a RESERVE, and IMPACT credite §2 pairs each settlement with a RESERVE. With no reservation, nothing can be refunded or consumed, so no money is created or destroyed.

decisions.question: What happens when a RESERVE exists but the wallet's reserved amount is below it (a drifted wallet)? LIVE-11 proposed releasing min(reserved, cost).
decisions.chosen_default: No partial release. The wallet update is conditional on reserved >= amount. If it does not match, commit the slot transition, write no ledger row, return credit='SKIPPED_WALLET_DRIFT' and log an error. The daily ledger check then reports the slot as an unsettled terminal slot and alerts admins. No automatic correction tool.
decisions.why_safe: A partial release would leave the ledger amount different from the wallet movement and hide the drift. Skipping keeps the ledger truthful, the job stops failing forever, and a human is alerted. It does not lock in any refund policy.

decisions.question: Which firms are exempt from the ledger-vs-wallet balance identity? seed-demo creates balances with no GRANT row.
decisions.chosen_default: Skip only the balance identity, and only for firms whose members are all @demo.ro users (the same convention prisma/cleanup-demo.ts uses). The reserved identity and the per-slot settlement rules still run for every firm. Skipped firms are counted in the report.
decisions.why_safe: This only affects detection, never money. The exemption is as narrow as possible: a real firm with at least one non-demo member is always checked. It is documented in IMPACT credite §7 in the Codex.

decisions.question: When does the daily check run and how are admins alerted?
decisions.chosen_default: Repeatable job 'ledger-check' on the existing reconciliation queue, pattern '40 3 * * *' with tz Europe/Bucharest, plus a one-off 'startup-ledger-check' at boot. On a mismatch: logger.error, plus one outbox event 'credits.ledger_mismatch' per day (eventKey credits.ledger_mismatch:YYYY-MM-DD) to every ADMIN with deletedAt null. Bell only, no email.
decisions.why_safe: Operations alert only. It extends the existing reconciliation worker as docs/18:64 asks, runs only on the active slot through activeOnlyProviders, and moves no money.

decisions.question: Accept path: losers used to be closed with an unconditional update. Does the switch to a conditional transition change behaviour?
decisions.chosen_default: settle() uses from=[loser.status as read under FOR UPDATE], so ACTIVE leads to REFUND and OFFER_SENT leads to CONSUME, exactly as today. claim.withdrawn is sent only for losers that actually settled, and refunded comes from the settle result.
decisions.why_safe: The outcome is the same under Serializable + FOR UPDATE (IMPACT credite §3/§8). The change only adds the conditional ticket as a backstop.

decisions.question: Should failed BullMQ jobs raise an admin alert (LIVE-11 proposed fix)?
decisions.chosen_default: Not in this package. The hourly sweep already retries failed SLA jobs (rearm → job.retry()), and /admin/jobs lists them.
decisions.why_safe: No behaviour change. This belongs to an observability package.

  export type TerminalClaimSlotStatus = Exclude<ClaimSlotStatus,'ACTIVE'|'OFFER_SENT'>;
  export type SettlementCreditOutcome = 'REFUND'|'CONSUME';
  export type SettlementQuotes = 'WITHDRAWN'|'SUPERSEDED'|'CHAT_READ_ONLY'|'KEEP';
  export interface SettleArgs {
    claimSlotId; from: ClaimSlotStatus[]; to: TerminalClaimSlotStatus; outcome: SettlementCreditOutcome;
    reason: CreditSettlementReason;
    where?: Prisma.ClaimSlotWhereInput;  // filtre atomice suplimentare
    quotes: SettlementQuotes;
    slot?: { companyId; requestId; claimCostCreditsSnapshot };  // evita o recitire (latenta cross-region)
  }
  export type SettleResult =
    | { settled: false }
    | { settled: true; slot: {id,companyId,requestId,claimCostCreditsSnapshot};
        credit: 'REFUNDED'|'CONSUMED'|'SKIPPED_NO_RESERVE'|'SKIPPED_ALREADY_SETTLED'|'SKIPPED_WALLET_DRIFT';
        refunded: boolean; amount: number }
settle(tx, args), in order:
 (1) tx.claimSlot.updateMany({ where: { ...args.where, id, status: { in: from } }, data: { status: to, ...(to === 'COMPLETED' ? {} : { withdrawnAt: new Date() }) } }). If count===0, return { settled:false }. Note that COMPLETED must NOT get withdrawnAt, same as fulfillment today.
 (2) Read the slot (findUniqueOrThrow with the select above) unless args.slot was passed.
 (3) Handle quotes: WITHDRAWN or SUPERSEDED → closeOpenQuotesForSlot(tx, id, mode) from claims/claims.helpers (this also makes the chat read-only); CHAT_READ_ONLY → tx.chatThread.updateMany({ where: { claimSlotId }, data: { readOnly: true } }); KEEP → nothing.
 (4) Ledger check: tx.creditTransaction.findMany({ where: { claimSlotId: id, type: { in: ['RESERVE','REFUND','CONSUME'] } }, select: { type, amount } }).
   - No RESERVE → credit SKIPPED_NO_RESERVE, amount 0, logger.warn.
   - A REFUND or CONSUME already exists → SKIPPED_ALREADY_SETTLED, logger.error.
   - Otherwise amount = RESERVE.amount (ledger truth; logger.warn if it differs from the snapshot). Call this.credits.refund or this.credits.consume, the only allowed call site. A false return → SKIPPED_WALLET_DRIFT with logger.error; true → REFUNDED or CONSUMED.
   Log only ids and amounts; use safeErrorSummary for errors.
 (5) Return refunded = (credit === 'REFUNDED').
The caller must already hold SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the request inside runTx 'claim' (invariant 3.1). State this in the header comment.

plan.summary:
E-company-21 (Sprint 22) plan. Neither docs/03 nor docs/07 settles the two open policy questions, so the plan doesn't pick a business answer for either one.

1. Claim cost: move the credit value and the min/max claim cost into system_settings (credit_value_ron=1000, claim_cost_min=1, claim_cost_max=0 meaning no cap). The defaults give exactly today's result. One shared resolver/formula is used by SizingService, the admin sizing preview, the public firm-rules page and the admin note. The admin rejects a max below the min.
2. Credit expiry: not built, pending a PO decision. The rule in docs/03 4.16 stays. There is no EXPIRE type, no job and no Terms change. The wallet only states what the code already does: credits can be used only while a subscription is active.
3. Admin weights page: already exists (/admin/sizing, E-admin-platform-25), so no new page. The admin note now shows the live credit value and cost range.

Migration: data-only (3 INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). No schema or enum change.
modules: packages/shared (request.schemas: claim cost rules + formula; legal FirmRulesDto)
FE admin (settings + sizing pages, new ClaimCostNote)
tables: system_settings (3 new rows: credit_value_ron, claim_cost_min, claim_cost_max; data-only)
requests (credit_cost written at publish/edit via new formula; no schema change)
project_sizing_config (read only)
project_size_thresholds (read only)
assumptions: The cost of a claim is still the PO r5 V1 rule (docs/archive/15-feedback-po-r5-sprints.md, docs/04 line 5): ceil(baseScore*BUDGET_RON_PER_POINT / credit value), at least 1 credit. The D-v6-5 seed 1/2/4 is legacy and its column project_size_thresholds.credit_cost stays dead. It is not revived.

The 3..25 clamp and 'credits never expire' appear only in the PO pricing proposals from September 2026 (auto-memory / pricing artifact). They are not recorded in docs/03 or docs/07, so they are not treated as decisions.
SubscriptionActiveGuard already blocks claims without an ACTIVE, unexpired subscription. Leftover credits of a lapsed firm are unusable today, whatever the expiry decision.
GET /billing/subscription returns null exactly when the firm has no active subscription. The wallet uses that as the 'no active subscription' signal.

Changing the new settings reprices only requests published or edited afterwards. The existing requests.credit_cost and the claim_slots.claim_cost_credits_snapshot are never recalculated (IMPACT credite rule 6, same as for sizing weights).

SizingService.compute runs outside the publish/edit transaction, so reading the settings in the same Promise.all adds no transaction time. It is one extra parallel query (the cross-region latency constraint).

Other Sprint 22 packages may add migrations. The implementer picks a timestamp later than the newest folder in apps/backend/prisma/migrations at write time (the newest today is 20261001011000_wallet_check_validate).
Blue/green: the migration is additive data only and the old slot ignores the keys, so it is safe on both slots.

decisions.question: Do credits expire 3 months after the subscription ends (docs/03 4.16)? Keep it (EXPIRE transaction type, daily job with 30/7-day warnings, wallet text, Terms clause with version bump and re-acceptance), move it post-MVP, or drop it (delete 4.16)?
decisions.chosen_default: No expiry is implemented. There is no EXPIRE enum value, no job, no CREDITS_EXPIRED thrower, and the Terms stay unchanged. The docs/03 4.16 rule is kept as written, with an implementation note marking it 'DECIZIE NECESARA PO: neimplementat; creditele nu expira in cod; se folosesc doar cu abonament activ'. The wallet only states the existing fact: credits can be used only while a subscription is active. Nothing is written into docs/07.
decisions.why_safe: The status quo never destroys purchased credits, so it is more generous than 4.16 and fully reversible. Building expiry now would permanently add a Postgres enum value, change the ledger-check formula and remove paid value from firms before the PO rules on it. docs/17:245 lists this as an open PO question, and the Sept pricing proposal argues for no expiry. No UI or Terms text today promises either outcome.

decisions.question: What minimum and maximum number of credits can one claim cost (the proposal says 3..25; today it is min 1 with no maximum)?
decisions.chosen_default: New system_settings keys: claim_cost_min=1 and claim_cost_max=0, where 0 means no cap. This gives the same cost as the current formula for every request. The admin can set a real cap from Admin > Settings without a deploy, and the value is validated: max is 0 or at least min.
decisions.why_safe: Zero behaviour or pricing change until the PO sets the numbers. The mechanism the package asks for exists and is testable (done_when #2 is proven by setting the key locally and in unit tests). No business number is invented.

decisions.question: What value does one credit have in lei of the minimum estimated budget?
decisions.chosen_default: credit_value_ron=1000, the PO r5 V1 rule (docs/archive/15, docs/04 line 5). It is now a system_settings key with the shared CREDIT_VALUE_RON constant kept as fallback/default.
decisions.why_safe: Same value as today. It only makes an already-decided rule configurable, which D-v6-5 ('configurabil din Admin') expects.

decisions.question: Is a new read-only admin page for project_sizing_config needed?
decisions.chosen_default: No new page. /admin/sizing (E-admin-platform-25) already shows and edits the weights with a preview and an audit trail. The only additions are the claim-cost note (credit value + range) on /admin/sizing and in Admin > Settings > Thresholds, and the preview now applies the clamp.
decisions.why_safe: It reuses a shipped, audited feature. The finding's evidence that no admin sizing route exists is stale.

decisions.question: Should a change to the credit value or the clamp reprice requests already in the marketplace?
decisions.chosen_default: No. The new rules apply at the next publish or edit. Claim slots keep claim_cost_credits_snapshot.
decisions.why_safe: It matches docs/03 4.5 (the snapshot is frozen at claim), IMPACT credite rule 6 and the behaviour of sizing weight edits. Nothing moves money retroactively.

decisions.question: Should the public 'Rules for firms' page show the claim cost range?
decisions.chosen_default: Show the sentence only when a real limit exists (claim_cost_max>0 or claim_cost_min>1). With the defaults the page is unchanged. The Terms of service are not touched.
decisions.why_safe: It follows the IMPACT credite rule 13 transparency pattern (the public page shows the setting in force). It is conditional, so the defaults change no public text, and it needs no terms-version bump.

close.commit_message:
feat(credits): settle-once claim credits, ledger check and configurable claim cost (Sprint 22)

- billing: ClaimSettlementService.settle() is now the only refund/consume path.
  The ledger decides the outcome (REFUNDED/CONSUMED/SKIPPED_*), and refund and
  consume are conditional on reserved >= amount. An ESLint rule bans direct
  credits.refund/consume calls.
- claims/quotes/requests/fulfillment: every settlement call site goes through
  settle(). refunded now reflects the real outcome. Fixes LIVE-11: SLA jobs on
  slots with no RESERVE no longer fail forever.
- db: partial unique indexes (one RESERVE and one REFUND/CONSUME per slot),
  VALIDATE on the wallet *_nonneg checks, and a data-only migration for
  credit_value_ron / claim_cost_min / claim_cost_max. Defaults keep today's
  pricing.
- ops: daily ledger-vs-wallet check on the reconciliation queue, a read-only
  GET /admin/credits/ledger-check, and a credits.ledger_mismatch admin bell.
- sizing/admin/legal/fe: one shared claim-cost formula, admin cost note,
  wallet note for firms without an active subscription, cost range on
  /firm-rules only when a limit exists. RO/EN i18n.

Open PO decisions: drifted wallet policy, claim_cost min/max values, credit
expiry (docs/03 4.16).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
decisions_needed: DECIZIE NECESARA (PO): what to do with a drifted wallet, where a RESERVE exists but the wallet's reserved is below the amount. Today there is no partial release and no automatic correction: the slot's status change is committed, no ledger row is written, and the daily ledger check alerts admins. Still open: whether there is a manual or automatic repair, and who absorbs the difference.

DECIZIE NECESARA (PO): the claim_cost_min / claim_cost_max values. The 3..25 proposal is not recorded in docs/03 or docs/07. The defaults stay at 1 / 0 (no cap), which is today's pricing, and the values can be set from Admin > Settings without a deploy.

DECIZIE NECESARA (PO): credit expiry (docs/03 4.16, credits valid 3 months after the subscription ends). It is not implemented. Options: keep it (EXPIRE type, daily job, 30/7-day warnings, Terms clause with a version bump), move it post-MVP, or drop it.

Operator step before deploying to prod: run the duplicate-RESERVE, duplicate-settlement and negative-wallet pre-check queries (they are in the migration headers and the CHANGELOG) before applying 20261001010000 and 20261001011000. Prod runs with RUN_MIGRATIONS=false, so apply them after a backup.

plan.summary: Plan for E-company-22 (Sprint 23). There is one backend bug fix: the dashboard computes available credits as balance - reserved, which subtracts reservations twice, so it becomes balance, with a unit test. The Stripe Checkout gets a locale and an EN/RO product description taken from the user's language preference. It is stored in the existing JSONB checkout attempt, so no migration is needed. Everything else is frontend work on the wallet page: metrics become Disponibile / Rezervate în preluări / Total deținut; employees get a read-only wallet with no purchase, order or payment-instructions queries; suspended and unapproved firms see AccessBlocked (the penalties card stays); FORBIDDEN gets a message in Billing.apiErrors and purchase errors show inside the confirm dialog; the RO 'Trial' label becomes 'Perioadă de probă'; money goes through one shared helper (2 fixed decimals plus a localized unit, lei in RO and RON in EN); IBAN, amount and reference get copy buttons. The penalty rule labels (Penalties.rule.*) already exist from E-company-9, so only the font-mono and raw-key styling of that list gets cleaned up. The docs contain no decision that blocks this package.

assumptions: Wallet semantics are fixed by credits.service.ts comments (4.8): balance = free credits, reserved = held by active claims, total held = balance + reserved. getWallet already returns available = balance. Only dashboardStats is wrong.

Penalty rule labels are already done: Penalties.rule.{SLA_MISS,MASS_SLA_MISS,VOLUNTARY_WITHDRAWAL} exist in RO and EN, and wallet/page.tsx:444 already uses tp.has('rule.'+key). F4-23's penalty-label part only needs the styling cleanup (drop font-mono on the list, keep the raw-key fallback).

The currency unit is already localized in existing messages: RO uses 'lei' (Billing.payButton, vatLine) and EN uses 'RON'. The shared helper follows that through a Common.money ICU key instead of hardcoding ' lei' in TSX.
The invoice PDF (invoice-pdf.service.ts money() = 2 decimals + 'RON') is a fiscal document governed by the ro-invoice skill ('moneda RON'). It stays unchanged; this package only aligns the UI.

GET /companies/me has no CompanyApprovedGuard, so useMyCompany().data.myRole is available for suspended and unapproved firms. GET /penalties/me also works for them, so the penalties card can stay visible under AccessBlocked.

Employees (EMPLOYEE_TRUSTED / EMPLOYEE_MANAGED) may see the balance, subscription and plans (docs and Codex: 'wallet-ul si planurile le vede toata echipa'), but not orders, invoices, payment instructions or purchases (CompanyManagerGuard). No backend permission change is needed.
Stripe Checkout supports locale 'ro' and 'en'. Replayed stripe_checkout_attempt rows saved before this change have no locale, which falls back to Stripe 'auto', the current behaviour.

The copied amount is the number without the unit, in 2-decimal format for the active locale (e.g. '121,00' in RO), matching what the user sees. IBAN is copied with whitespace removed. The reference copies the full 'Comanda XXXXXXXX' string shown on screen.

decisions.question: Should the dashboard 'Disponibile' be balance or balance - reserved?
decisions.chosen_default: available = balance (free credits), identical to GET /billing/wallet. Reserved is shown separately, and Total deținut = balance + reserved.
decisions.why_safe: credits.service.ts header (semantica 4.8) and CONCEPT credite si bani define balance as free credits and total held as balance + reserved. Pure display fix, no ledger change.

decisions.question: Should employees see the wallet at all, and what can they see?
decisions.chosen_default: Read-only wallet: balance metrics, subscription status and plans (no buy buttons), penalties. Orders, bank transfer and purchases are hidden. The note 'Doar proprietarul sau un manager poate cumpăra.' is shown.
decisions.why_safe: Mirrors the existing server rule (CompanyManagerGuard on orders, payment-instructions and purchases; wallet, subscription and plans open to the whole team, per BE billing and CONCEPT autorizare). No permission change.

decisions.question: Money format: which unit and decimals in the UI?
decisions.chosen_default: Always 2 fixed decimals, with the unit from Common.money ('{amount} lei' in RO, '{amount} RON' in EN, matching the existing Billing templates). The invoice PDF stays as is ('RON', 2 decimals).
decisions.why_safe: Presentation only. It follows the convention already in the RO and EN messages and does not change any amount, rounding or fiscal document.

decisions.question: Stripe Checkout language and product name
decisions.chosen_default: Pass locale ('ro'|'en') from users.language_preference, the same source already used for the return URLs. Build the product description in RO or EN with the same data (credits, tier, SUBSCRIPTION_DAYS).
decisions.why_safe: The page language and the item label change; the amount, currency, expiry and idempotency do not. Old saved attempts replay without locale, which is today's behaviour.

decisions.question: What should suspended or unapproved firms see on the wallet?
decisions.chosen_default: When /billing/wallet or /billing/subscription errors with COMPANY_SUSPENDED or COMPANY_NOT_APPROVED, show AccessBlocked (existing component, CTA to /company) instead of the wallet and subscription sections. Keep the penalties card (it still loads and explains the suspension end date).
decisions.why_safe: Reuses the existing blocked-state component and codes (FE marketplace firma: AccessBlocked on SUBSCRIPTION_INACTIVE / COMPANY_NOT_APPROVED / COMPANY_SUSPENDED). No rule change.

assumptions: E-admin-platform-4 already delivered buyer_snapshot (column, the write in confirm(), and reads in the PDF and CSV with a live fallback for old rows). This package extends it; it does not recreate it.

Local DB: 6 CONFIRMED orders. 5 have buyer_snapshot and 1 (a subscription) does not. Demo company 'A Mobila Premium' has cui stored as 'RO7850265', because the seed bypasses normalizeCui. The local seller data is valid (confirmations work) and Stripe is disabled locally (no STRIPE_SECRET_KEY), so local orders go through bank transfer plus admin confirm.
The VAT-payer field was accepted as a data-model change in the approved package risks. docs/04 must be updated in the same sprint.
A CUI stored or typed with the RO prefix counts as a VAT-payer declaration. This reuses the onboarding behaviour that the zod schema already accepts but normalizeCui currently throws away.

Orders confirmed before this change have NULL service_period_*. Their description stays as it is today, with the tier and without a period; the period is not reconstructed.

decisions.question: For invoices already issued (buyer_snapshot IS NULL), do we freeze the firm's current data as their buyer snapshot, or leave them unchanged (live read at download)?
decisions.chosen_default: Leave them unchanged. Do not backfill; the live fallback (buyerFromCompany with withDeletedRecords) stays for rows without a snapshot. The ready-to-run backfill SQL goes in the brief and in CHANGELOG as a pending PO decision, and is not executed.
decisions.why_safe: Issued fiscal documents are not modified. The prisma-migration skill says snapshots are written once at the event, and a backfill would stamp today's data as if it were issue-time data. It can still be done later with one idempotent UPDATE if the PO chooses to freeze.

decisions.question: How is a firm's VAT-payer status established and kept current: self-declared (RO prefix at onboarding plus an OWNER/MANAGER toggle through PATCH /companies/me), verified against the ANAF public API at onboarding and approval, or set by admin only?
decisions.chosen_default: Self-declared. Onboarding sets is_vat_payer when the typed CUI starts with RO. OWNER/MANAGER can change it through PATCH /companies/me, and that call is audited as COMPANY_PROFILE_UPDATED. No ANAF API call and no new UI toggle; the company dashboard only shows the flag.
decisions.why_safe: No external integration and no business rule is locked in. The firm is already responsible for its own fiscal data at onboarding, and the change is audited, so ANAF verification can be added later without a schema change.

decisions.question: Existing companies whose stored cui already starts with 'RO' (seed and legacy rows): should they be flagged as VAT payers?
decisions.chosen_default: Yes. The migration backfills is_vat_payer = true WHERE cui ~* '^RO'. Stored cui values are not rewritten.
decisions.why_safe: These firms' invoices print exactly what they print today ('RO…'), with no regression. Onboarded firms had RO stripped, so they stay false until they declare.

decisions.question: What unit and quantity go on the invoice line?
decisions.chosen_default: 1 × 'buc', unit price excluding VAT = base amount, for both subscriptions and credit packages.
decisions.why_safe: Presentation only. Base, VAT and total are unchanged, and there is no rounding drift from splitting a package into per-credit prices.

decisions.question: Should the IBAN still be printed on card-paid invoices?
decisions.chosen_default: Print the IBAN only when payment_source = 'admin' (bank transfer), as approved in package step 4. It stays in seller_snapshot per docs/03 §4.17.
decisions.why_safe: The stored snapshot is unchanged and follows the approved step. Art. 319 does not require the IBAN on an invoice that is already paid.

decisions.question: Which end date is printed for the subscription service period?
decisions.chosen_default: 'perioada {start} – {end}', where end is the Bucharest date of the new expires_at and start = expires_at - 30 days.
decisions.why_safe: It mirrors grantOrExtend exactly (D-L0-2 extend semantics), and no duration changes.

plan.summary: Implementation plan for E-company-24 (Sprint 23, P2, ~2.5 days). The work: (1) billing emails and in-app notifications go only to OWNER/MANAGER; (2) MailService gets attachment support, and the invoice PDF is attached to payment.confirmed; (3) a new firm-facing event, payment.transfer_instructions, emails the IBAN, amount and reference plus a proforma PDF with no fiscal number when a bank order is created while Stripe is off, and a new GET /billing/orders/:id/proforma endpoint serves the same proforma; (4) a new "Am plătit" action (POST /billing/orders/:id/mark-paid) that notifies admins; (5) an hourly sweep that sends a reminder and then auto-cancels stale bank orders. The sweep is controlled by two new system_settings keys that default to 0 (off) until the PO picks N, and it never touches orders the firm has marked as paid; (6) the buy-credits hint depends on stripeEnabled, and the bankTransfer.missing text is made truthful; (7) an optional companies.billing_email for the accountant, which receives the proforma and invoice once per event, tracked by a durable marker. The OP-proof upload and the "pay by OP alongside Stripe" option are left out. The code was read at its current state. The evidence line numbers in the plan are stale, but every finding still reproduces: the payment.confirmed and subscription.expiring targets are all company_members, EMAILED_EVENTS lacks payment.pending, only the Stripe expired event cancels PENDING orders, buyCreditsHint always mentions Stripe, and MailService.send has no attachments. Locally, Stripe is off and billing is ready, so the bank path can be tested end to end with owner.a@demo.ro and Mailpit on :8025.

The reference the firm writes on the transfer stays the existing FE shortRef: id.slice(0,8).toUpperCase(), shown as 'Comanda {REF}'. The admin payments list already shows the same '#REF', so proforma, email and UI must use exactly that string.

The proforma is not a fiscal document. It takes no number from invoice_series, and 4.17 plus the ro-invoice skill number invoices only at confirm(). It carries 'Factură proformă nr. {REF}', the order date (Europe/Bucharest), the live seller from BillingReadinessService.assertReady() including the IBAN, the live buyer (buyerFromCompany), invoiceDescription(), base+VAT+total from the order snapshot, and the note 'Document fără valoare fiscală — factura se emite după confirmarea plății'.

Blocked or soft-deleted members are excluded from billing targets (user.deletedAt null, user.blockedAt null).

The existing admin-only payment.pending event stays unchanged. checkout-recovery.integration.spec counts it per company, so the firm-facing email uses a distinct event type, payment.transfer_instructions.

PDF rendering happens inside the notifications worker (active slot only) with the existing Puppeteer browser. If rendering fails, the email is still sent without the attachment and with the wallet link; only SMTP failures throw (retry per recipient).

The accountant copy (companies.billing_email) gets only the document emails, payment.transfer_instructions (proforma) and payment.confirmed (invoice). decisions.question: After how many days should an unpaid bank-transfer order be reminded, and after how many should it be auto-cancelled? Calendar or working days? What happens to a transfer that arrives after auto-cancel (no reopen exists; confirm on CANCELLED = 409)?
decisions.chosen_default: Two new system_settings keys, bank_transfer_reminder_days and bank_transfer_expiry_days, both '0' (0 = off). They are seeded by the migration and seed.ts, editable in Admin -> Setari, and validated as integers 0..365. Calendar days from created_at. The reminder is skipped when reminderDays >= expiryDays (expiry>0). Orders the firm marked as paid (payment_claimed_at set) are never reminded or auto-cancelled.
decisions.why_safe: No duration is invented and nothing irreversible happens until the PO sets a value. Auto-cancel is irreversible (a late transfer would need manual handling), so it stays off by default. The same pattern is already used for expired_offer_autoclose_enabled=false. The machinery is fully testable locally by setting the keys.

decisions.question: Should firms be able to choose 'Plătesc prin OP' (bank transfer) while Stripe is enabled?
decisions.chosen_default: No. Bank transfer remains only the fallback when the Stripe keys are missing; payment-instructions keeps returning bankTransfer only when Stripe is off.
decisions.why_safe: docs/07 D-L0-1 (FINAL) says Stripe is the primary channel and bank transfer plus admin confirmation is the fallback when Stripe keys are missing.

decisions.question: Attach the invoice PDF to the email, or send a short-lived signed download link?
decisions.chosen_default: Attach the PDF (nodemailer attachments). No new public or unauthenticated endpoint, no token handling; the wallet link stays in the email as a fallback.
decisions.why_safe: This is a technical choice, not a business rule. It avoids a new @Public route that would expose fiscal documents behind a bearer URL (invariant 3.4 prefers auth-checked presigned GETs).

decisions.question: Does the proforma consume a number from the fiscal invoice series, or have its own series?
decisions.chosen_default: No fiscal number. The proforma is identified by the order reference 'Comanda {REF}' and labeled 'Document fără valoare fiscală'.
decisions.why_safe: docs/03 4.17 and the ro-invoice skill: the SERIE-NUMĂR is continuous and allocated only at confirmed payment, so a proforma must not burn numbers.

decisions.question: Should employees keep the in-app bell for payment.confirmed and subscription.expiring?
decisions.chosen_default: No. Targets are OWNER/MANAGER only, for both bell and email (package acceptance: 'go only to OWNER/MANAGER'). recipientsFor also filters by role as defense in depth for outbox rows already queued.
decisions.why_safe: Employees get 403 on orders and invoices and cannot buy. The team still sees subscription status through the dashboard banner.

decisions.question: Which emails should the optional company billing email (accountant) receive?
decisions.chosen_default: Only document emails: proforma at bank-order start and invoice at confirmation. Once per event (durable marker), no unsubscribe link, Reply-To = support.
decisions.why_safe: It is opt-in by the firm's OWNER/MANAGER and carries only billing documents, never project content. Adding reminders later is a one-line change.

decisions.question: Should 'Am plătit' accept an OP (payment order) upload as proof?
decisions.chosen_default: Not in this package. 'Am plătit' only timestamps payment_claimed_at and notifies admins in-app (payment.marked_paid).
decisions.why_safe: Upload needs a new attachment entityType plus AV scanning and presign rules (CONCEPT uploads); the finding marks it optional. Admins confirm against the bank statement as today.

plan.brief:
PACKAGE E-admin-platform-58 - "Pricing data model (P3)". Goal: plans and plan features become editable data with one entitlements service, WITHOUT changing any price, credit amount, duration or rule. Read first: .claude/skills/prisma-migration, nestjs-module and ui-component SKILL.md; Codex notes "50 Impact/IMPACT schema Prisma", "IMPACT endpoint nou", "IMPACT text UI", "IMPACT credite", "10 Module BE/BE billing", "COMMON guards"; docs/03 4.8/4.10/4.16; docs/07 Î7/Î8/D-v6-5/D-L0-1/D-L0-2 (FINAL - do not edit docs/07).

OUT OF SCOPE (do not do):
- Writing any pricing decision in docs/07.
- Changing seed prices, credits or trial values.
- Stripe recurring billing (stays mode 'payment' + grantOrExtend 30 days).
- Registering Ofertare Rapida / AI-read features.
- Claim-cost clamp code: it already exists (E-company-21), only verify it.

STEP 0 - Baseline
Snapshot the plan data, then record the test baseline.
```
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select id,tier,price_ron,included_credits,marketplace_gating_delay_minutes,is_active from subscription_plans"
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select company_id,plan_id,status,expires_at from subscriptions order by expires_at desc limit 20"
```
Save the output to the scratchpad for the restore. Record `pnpm -F backend test` pass counts.

STEP 1 - Schema + migration (follow IMPACT schema Prisma)

schema.prisma, SubscriptionPlan:
- `tier SubscriptionPlanTier? @unique`, with the comment "legacy; identitatea planului = code; DROP intr-un release separat".
- `code String @unique`
- `nameRo String? @map("name_ro")`
- `nameEn String? @map("name_en")`
- `features SubscriptionPlanFeature[]`

New model:
```prisma
model SubscriptionPlanFeature {
  planId     String   @map("plan_id")
  featureKey String   @map("feature_key")
  enabled    Boolean  @default(false)
  limitValue Int?     @map("limit_value")
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at") @db.Timestamptz()
  plan SubscriptionPlan @relation(fields: [planId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  @@id([planId, featureKey])
  @@map("subscription_plan_features")
}
```

Migration folder: `apps/backend/prisma/migrations/20261001060000_plans_as_data/` (first check `ls prisma/migrations | tail`; the timestamp must be unique and later than 20261001050000). Generate the diff with `pnpm -F backend exec prisma migrate diff --from-migrations prisma/migrations --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --shadow-database-url <DATABASE_URL>`. Then HAND-EDIT the SQL into this order:
1. `ALTER TABLE "subscription_plans" ADD COLUMN "code" TEXT, ADD COLUMN "name_ro" TEXT, ADD COLUMN "name_en" TEXT;`
2. `UPDATE "subscription_plans" SET "code" = "tier"::text WHERE "code" IS NULL;`
3. `ALTER TABLE "subscription_plans" ALTER COLUMN "code" SET NOT NULL;`
4. `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "subscription_plans_code_key" ON "subscription_plans"("code");`
5. `ALTER TABLE "subscription_plans" ALTER COLUMN "tier" DROP NOT NULL;`
6. `CREATE TABLE "subscription_plan_features" (...)` with the PK(plan_id, feature_key) and the FK to subscription_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. The plan_id type must match subscription_plans.id, which is TEXT.
7. `INSERT INTO "subscription_plan_features"("plan_id","feature_key","enabled","updated_at") SELECT "id",'MARKETPLACE_ACCESS',true,now() FROM "subscription_plans" ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;`

Add a `-- Rollback:` comment:
1. Redeploy the previous image first.
2. Then `DROP TABLE subscription_plan_features`.
3. Then `UPDATE subscription_plans SET tier = code::subscription_plan_tier WHERE tier IS NULL AND code IN ('SILVER','GOLD','PLATINUM')`. Plans with other codes must be deactivated or deleted before `ALTER tier SET NOT NULL`.
4. Then `DROP code/name_ro/name_en`.

Also note in the SQL comment the blue/green caveat: the old slot ignores features, so during a rollback a plan with MARKETPLACE_ACCESS=false would still have access.

Apply and regenerate:
```
pnpm -F backend prisma migrate deploy && pnpm -F backend prisma generate
```
EPERM on the Windows dll while nest --watch runs is harmless.

Seeds:
- seed.ts: upsert plans by `code` (the 3 legacy codes, with tier set to the same value). Upsert the feature row MARKETPLACE_ACCESS=true. Prices and credits stay unchanged.
- seed-demo.ts: same wherever it looks up plans by tier (`where: { tier }` becomes `where: { code }`).

STEP 2 - Shared (packages/shared)

a) New `plan-features.ts`:
- `PLAN_FEATURE_KEYS = ['MARKETPLACE_ACCESS'] as const`
- `type PlanFeatureKey`
- `PLAN_FEATURE_DEFAULTS: Record<PlanFeatureKey, {enabled:false, limit:null}>`
- `type PlanFeaturesDto = Record<PlanFeatureKey, { enabled: boolean; limit: number | null }>`
- `PLAN_CODE_RE = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,31}$/`
- `type PlanCode = string`
- `resolvePlanFeatures(rows: {featureKey:string, enabled:boolean, limitValue:number|null}[]): PlanFeaturesDto`. It ignores unknown keys and falls back to the defaults.
- Export it from index.ts.

b) billing.schemas.ts:
- `SubscriptionPlanDto`: `tier: PlanCode` (was the enum) plus `nameRo: string|null`, `nameEn: string|null`, `isFree: boolean`, `vatRate: number`, `vatRon: number`, `totalRon: number`, `features: PlanFeaturesDto`.
- `CreditPackageDto`: add `vatRate`, `vatRon`, `totalRon`.
- `SubscriptionDetailDto.tier`, `AdminSubscriptionItemDto.tier`, `BillingOrderDto.planTier` and `AdminBillingOrderItemDto.planTier` all become `PlanCode` (field names unchanged; saved idempotency receipts stay valid).
- New `EntitlementsDto`: `{ planId: string|null; planCode: string|null; nameRo: string|null; nameEn: string|null; isFree: boolean; isTrial: boolean; expiresAt: string|null; gatingDelayMinutes: number|null; features: PlanFeaturesDto }`.

c) admin.schemas.ts:
- `AdminPlanDto { id, code, tier (=code), nameRo, nameEn, priceRon, includedCredits, marketplaceGatingDelayMin, isActive, isFree, features }`
- `AdminCreditPackageDto { id, credits, priceRon, isActive }`
- `AdminThresholdDto { id, size, minScore, maxScore|null }`
- `createPlanSchema = z.object({ code: z.string().regex(PLAN_CODE_RE), nameRo: z.string().trim().max(60).optional(), nameEn: ...same, priceRon: z.number().int().min(0).max(10_000_000), includedCredits: z.number().int().min(0).max(100000), marketplaceGatingDelayMin: z.number().int().min(0), isActive: z.boolean().optional(), features: z.object({ MARKETPLACE_ACCESS: z.object({ enabled: z.boolean() }) }) })`. `features` is REQUIRED so that access is an explicit choice.
- `updatePlanSchema`: priceRon `.min(0)` (was positive); add nameRo/nameEn (nullable optional) and `features` partial (per key `{enabled, limit?}`). `code` is immutable (not in the update schema).
- `AdminKpiDto`: add `activeSubscriptionsByPlan: { code: string; count: number }[]`.

d) New `company-permissions.ts`:
- `COMPANY_PERMISSIONS = ['BILLING_MANAGE','MEMBERS_MANAGE','COMPANY_PROFILE_EDIT','CLAIMS_ASSIGN'] as const`
- `COMPANY_ROLE_PERMISSIONS: Record<CompanyMemberRole, readonly CompanyPermission[]>`
- `can(role, permission)`

Fill the matrix ONLY from the current backend checks. BILLING_MANAGE = OWNER, MANAGER (company-manager.guard.ts). For the other three, read the enforcing code in companies.service.ts (member invite/remove/role change, profile/locations/portfolio/offer permissions) and claims.service.ts (assignment), and copy the role sets exactly.
