plan.summary: Sprint 74 plan for E-admin-platform-56 (P3, ~6 days), in execution order. (1) The public health routes return only {status}. Release, checks and client details appear only when the request carries an X-Health-Token header matching the new optional HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN. verify-slot, its tests, the container smoke and the runbook are updated to match. (2) An optional LISTEN_HOST setting, set to 127.0.0.1 in start-combined.sh. (3) A production-only X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow header on any host other than the NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL host. (4) A per-request nonce CSP built in middleware, with 'strict-dynamic'. connect-src and img-src are narrowed only when the new build arg NEXT_PUBLIC_STORAGE_ORIGIN is set. Also a same-origin /csp-report collector, COOP same-origin, and the release SHA kept out of the browser bundle unless Sentry is on. (5) Supply chain: nodemailer 10.0.9+ and an engine.io 6.6.10+ override fix the 2 HIGH advisories that currently fail the existing prod audit gate. Prisma moves to dependencies, the runtime image gets a prod-only dependency stage, and the dev tools are upgraded or overridden. CI gets a Trivy image scan (HIGH/CRITICAL with a fix available), contents: read permissions and SHA-pinned actions; Caddy is pinned by digest and a CodeQL workflow is added. (6) The NestJS 11 / Express 5 upgrade comes last, with a rule to revert it cleanly if the gates fail. No DB migration. Removing the Railway slot and alias domains is left to the PO and operator, because docs/07 does not decide it.
modules: backend: whole app for NestJS 11 / Express 5 upgrade (package.json, lockfile)
frontend: next.config.mjs headers (COOP, X-Robots-Tag, CSP removed from static headers)
docs: 08-deployment.md, implementation/blue-green-release.md, CHANGELOG.md, Codex vault notes
files: apps/backend/src/infra/mail/mail.service.ts (only if nodemailer 10 API changes require it)
assumptions: No Prisma schema or data change. The only DB touch is one read-only SELECT on inspiration_photos (production, run by the operator) to list the image hosts in use before narrowing img-src.

The implementer never changes Railway domains, variables or GitHub repo settings. Removing the slot domains, setting HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN / NEXT_PUBLIC_STORAGE_ORIGIN on both slots, and turning on secret scanning are operator or PO steps, documented in docs/08.
Railway's platform healthcheck (railway.json), the Caddy health_uri and the uptime monitor read only the HTTP status (and 'degraded' in /ready), so a status-only public body breaks none of them.
Older releases kept for rollback still return the full public body, so the new verify-slot must also accept a full body without a token.

`railway run` runs locally and cannot reach *.railway.internal. It is used only to inject HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN into verify-slot's environment. Slot verification still needs an HTTP URL: the slot domain today, a temporary domain after the PO decision.

Next 15 applies the nonce to its own scripts only during dynamic rendering, and only when the CSP (with nonce) is present on the forwarded request headers. next-intl forwards `new Headers(request.headers)` in both NextResponse.next and rewrite, so setting the headers on req before calling intl(req) is enough. The implementer must confirm this in the built container (every <script> in the HTML has nonce=).

Google Maps is injected by a bundled script via document.createElement, so 'strict-dynamic' allows it and the scripts it loads. styled-jsx in offer-builder.tsx needs style-src 'unsafe-inline', which stays.
Socket.IO connects same-origin (io() without a URL), so CSP3 'self' covers ws/wss on the same host.

`next build` on Windows fails at the standalone symlink step (known gotcha), so the production CSP, noindex, LISTEN_HOST and image checks are verified with a Docker build of Dockerfile.app plus tools/smoke-production-container.mjs.

The current prod audit already fails CI: `pnpm audit --prod` shows HIGH engine.io GHSA-2gc4-cqfq-p2gv (6.6.8) and HIGH nodemailer GHSA-v53p-9fqp-m79j (9.1.1). Fixing them belongs to step 4 of this package.
Dependabot already covers /deploy/gateway (the finding is stale on that point); only the Caddy digest pin is missing.

decisions.question: Can we remove the public Railway domains of app-blue, app-green and the old gateway alias (gateway-production-92ac), and verify releases only through a temporary domain created and deleted per release (plus HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN)?
decisions.chosen_default: Ship code that works either way: public health shows status only, details require the token, verify-slot reads the token from env, and X-Robots-Tag noindex applies on every non-canonical host. Leave the domains, and FRONTEND_PREVIEW_ORIGINS, in place. Add a runbook section 'Slot domains private' with the exact operator steps: generate a temporary domain, verify, delete the domain, drop FRONTEND_PREVIEW_ORIGINS, update playwright.green-ui.config.ts usage. The operator runs it only after the PO says yes.
decisions.why_safe: Nothing in production changes without the PO. The noindex header and the status-only health already remove the SEO duplicate and the SHA disclosure. The slots stay reachable for verify-slot and Playwright until the PO decides.

decisions.question: How should release details (slot/mode/sha/checks/client) be reached once public health returns only {status}?
decisions.chosen_default: Optional backend env HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN (min 32 chars). Details are returned only when the X-Health-Token header matches (constant-time compare on sha256 digests). Unset means details are never returned. The header is redacted in pino.
decisions.why_safe: Purely technical; closed by default. Rollback slots without the feature still return full bodies, which verify-slot accepts.

decisions.question: Admin inspiration photos accept any https imageUrl (IsUrl, no host allowlist). Should they be limited to an allowlist or uploaded to storage, now that CSP img-src is narrowed?
decisions.chosen_default: Narrow img-src and connect-src only when the build arg NEXT_PUBLIC_STORAGE_ORIGIN is set. Allowlist: 'self', data:, blob:, the storage origin(s), maps.googleapis.com, maps.gstatic.com, *.googleapis.com / *.gstatic.com as needed by Places, cdn.prod.website-files.com, and extra origins from NEXT_PUBLIC_CSP_IMG_ORIGINS. When unset, keep the current broad `https:` for img/connect. Before the operator sets the arg, run the read-only host query on inspiration_photos and add every host found.
decisions.why_safe: No image or upload breaks on deploy. Narrowing is switched on by a deliberate rebuild after the PO answers. Nonce, strict-dynamic, reporting and COOP ship regardless.

decisions.question: Where should CSP violation reports go?
decisions.chosen_default: A same-origin Next route /csp-report that logs one sanitized console.warn line per report to the Railway logs. It keeps only the directive, the blocked origin and the masked document path; it has a 16 KB cap, 60 reports per minute per process, and always answers 204. No third party.
decisions.why_safe: No new processor or DPA, and no personal data: paths are masked with maskPath and query strings are dropped.

decisions.question: A nonce CSP makes every [locale] page dynamically rendered (the landing page is no longer static). Is that acceptable?
decisions.chosen_default: Accept it; the package risks already name it. Measure TTFB for /ro, /en and /en/studio in the container smoke before and after, and report the numbers in the CHANGELOG. Invent no threshold.
decisions.why_safe: The approved package already accepts this risk. The operator tries it on the standby slot before promotion.

decisions.question: What should the image-scan gate fail on?
decisions.chosen_default: Trivy vuln scanner, severity HIGH,CRITICAL, --ignore-unfixed, exit 1. Exceptions only in .trivyignore.yaml, each with a statement and an expired_at date of at most 90 days. Trivy runs as a digest-pinned aquasec/trivy container image, not through a tag-pinned action.
decisions.why_safe: Technical CI policy; unfixed OS CVEs give no actionable fix, and pinning by digest avoids the mutable-tag supply-chain risk this package is fixing.

decisions.question: Should GitHub secret scanning and push protection be turned on?
decisions.chosen_default: Add the CodeQL workflow in the repo. Document secret scanning and push protection as a PO toggle in GitHub Settings > Code security. The implementer changes no repo settings.
decisions.why_safe: Repository settings belong to the owner. CodeQL is a file in the repo and free for public repos.

IMPLEMENTER BRIEF — E-admin-platform-56 "Hide internal slot addresses and patch dependencies" (Sprint 74, P3)

No migration, no i18n keys (no UI text changes). Hard rules: no git commit/push/stash/checkout/reset, never edit apps/backend/.env, and touch no Railway or GitHub settings. Comments in Romanian without diacritics.

=== STEP 1 (do_first) — Public health shows status only (SEC2-9) ===
1a. apps/backend/src/config/config.schema.ts: add
   HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN: z.preprocess(v => typeof v === 'string' && v.trim() === '' ? undefined : v, z.string().min(32).optional()),
   Comment: "token pentru detaliile health (slot/mode/sha/checks/client); nesetat = detaliile nu se dau niciodata". Keep it optional in production as well, so a slot that lacks the variable still boots. Add a config.schema.spec.ts case: '' → undefined, 'short' → fails, 32 chars → ok.
1b. health.controller.ts:
   - Inject the config (already present). Add `private detailsAllowed(req?: Request): boolean`. It reads `this.config.get<string>('HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN')` and returns false when the token is unset or `req` is missing. Otherwise it compares `createHash('sha256').update(header).digest()` with the digest of the token using `timingSafeEqual` (import from 'node:crypto'). The header comes from `req.headers['x-health-token']` and must be a string; for arrays, use false.
   - check(@Req() req?): run the checks as today. The 503 path stays as it is (the exception filter already strips `checks`). On 200: `if (!this.detailsAllowed(req)) return { status: 'ok' };` else return the current full object (status, checks, release, client, timestamp).
   - live(@Req() req?): public `{ status: 'ok' }`; with the token → `{ status, release, timestamp }`.
   - ready(@Req() req?): public `{ status: 'ok' | 'degraded' }`; with the token → the current body. The 503 for DB down stays.
   - Update the header comments: the public body is status only, details need X-Health-Token (E-admin-platform-56).
1c. apps/backend/src/app.module.ts pino redact: add 'req.headers["x-health-token"]'.
1d. health.controller.spec.ts: setup() gets an optional token value. Update the existing tests to pass a request with the header where they assert release/checks/client. New tests:
   (i) without a token configured, check()/live()/ready() bodies are exactly {status:'ok'} and {status:'degraded'} (use toEqual). JSON.stringify must not contain the SHA.
   (ii) configured token + wrong header → minimal body.
   (iii) configured token + correct header → full body with release.sha.
   (iv) header as array → minimal.
   (v) ready() degraded stays minimal without the token.
1e. apps/backend/.env.example: add a commented `# HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN=` with its explanation (no value).

=== STEP 2 — verify-slot, smoke tool, runbook ===
2a. tools/release/verify-slot.mjs:
   - Read the token ONLY from `process.env.HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN` (never argv, to keep it out of shell history). Pass it into verifySlot as `healthToken`.
   - Send it as the header `X-Health-Token` on the FIRST /api/v1/health request and on the /health/live probe. The rate-limit probe requests stay without the token.
   - If `health.release` is missing and the body is exactly {status:'ok'}, throw: 'Health details hidden: run with HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN (e.g. railway run --service <slot> node tools/release/verify-slot.mjs ...)'.
   - A full body without a token (older rollback releases) is still accepted.
   - Never print the token; the result object must not include it.
2b. tools/release/verify-slot.test.mjs: the fake server returns the minimal body unless the header matches. Tests:
   - token env → passes and the header is sent only on health and live;

close.commit_message:
feat(security): perimeter and supply chain hardening (Sprint 74, E-admin-platform-56)

- health: public body is {status} only; details behind X-Health-Token
  (HEALTH_DETAILS_TOKEN, constant-time compare, redacted in pino)
- backend listens on loopback in the combined container (LISTEN_HOST)
- frontend: per-request nonce CSP with 'strict-dynamic' in middleware,
  same-origin /csp-report collector, COOP same-origin, X-Robots-Tag
  noindex on non-canonical hosts, release SHA only with Sentry DSN
- supply chain: NestJS 11 / Express 5, nodemailer 10, engine.io
  override, prisma in dependencies, prod-only deps stage in image,
  pnpm audit 0 findings, Trivy HIGH/CRITICAL gate, SHA-pinned actions,
  CodeQL workflow, Caddy pinned by digest
- verify-slot: token from env only, sent only over https/loopback
- docs/08, blue-green runbook, CHANGELOG updated; no DB migration

allowlist, GitHub secret scanning.
